title: UN: Keep International Force in Lebanon to Protect Civilians
content:
The United Nations Security Council should ensure that an international force remains in southern Lebanon to protect civilians and deter human rights abuses by the Israeli military and Hezbollah, Human Rights Watch said today. 

In August 2025, the Security Council unanimously decided to extend the mandate of the UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), which first deployed in 1978, one final time until the end of 2026, when it would begin a phased withdrawal. That decision came before the latest escalation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah in March 2026—and before Israeli forces displaced hundreds of thousands of civilians and occupied large swathes of southern Lebanon. Deliberate acts of displacement may amount to the war crime of forced displacement.

“Pulling the plug on UNIFIL without a robust international force in place would effectively abandon millions of Lebanese civilians to an uncertain and potentially disastrous fate,” said Louis Charbonneau, UN director at Human Rights Watch. “UN missions may not be a lasting solution, but the peacekeepers are a crucial deterrent against attacks on civilians and human rights abuses.”

title: Tapes Hidden in an Ice Cream Box Lay Bare a Maltese Journalist’s Assassination
content:
Secret audio recordings captured on a device hidden in a sock, along with text messages presented in a Maltese courtroom, laid bare the mechanics behind the 2017 assassination of journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia—linking a prominent tycoon to hitmen, cash payoffs, and high-level government leaks.

The recordings were played at the trial of Yorgen Fenech, the businessman accused of ordering the assassination. Caruana Galizia, 53, was killed by a car bomb placed beneath the driver’s seat of her vehicle and detonated remotely via SMS on the outskirts of Mosta.

Five men—George Degiorgio, Alfred Degiorgio, Vince Muscat, Robert Agius, and Jamie Vella—have all been convicted for their roles in the murder. Fenech denies any involvement and has pleaded not guilty.

The tapes were recorded by Melvin Theuma, a confessed middleman who was granted a presidential pardon in exchange for evidence. Theuma hid the recorder in his sock and began taping Fenech in April 2018, months after the hitmen were arrested.

“I started recording Yorgen because I needed the proof,” he told jurors. “I knew they were going to betray me either by killing me or throwing me in jail.”

title: The media has made Donald Trump look more coherent than he is. It’s called ‘sanewashing’
content:
On September 5 2024, after giving a speech about his economic plans for the United States, Donald Trump was asked what he would do, if re-elected president, to make childcare more affordable.

Trump then offered a nonsensical, 374-word response:

well, I would do that, and we’re sitting down – you know, I was somebody – we had Senator Marco Rubio, and my daughter, Ivanka, was so impactful on that issue. It’s a very important issue. But I think when you talk about the kind of numbers that I’m talking about – because, look, childcare is childcare. It’s something – you have to have it. In this country, you have to have it. But when you talk about those numbers compared to the kind of numbers that I’m talking about by taxing foreign nations at levels that they’re not used to – but they’ll get used to it very quickly. And it’s not going to stop them from doing business with us, but they’ll have a very substantial tax when they send product into our country […]

title: Hallitus linjasi sote-järjestöjen avustusten periaatteista – Adlercreutz: hallituksen sisäinen kiista saatiin nollattua
content:
Hallitus hyväksyi torstaina STEA-avustusten jakamista koskevan asetusmuutoksen, joka määrittää, millä periaatteilla sosiaali- ja terveysalan avustusrahat tulee jakaa.

Sosiaali- ja terveysministeri Wille Rydmanin (ps.) näkemyksen mukaan asetus ei ole ristiriidassa hänen aiemmin linjaamiensa avustuskriteerien kanssa. Hallituskumppanit olivat asiasta eri linjoilla.

Rydmanin mukaan asetukseen kirjattiin perusperiaate siitä, että avustusten jaossa painotetaan kohtaavaa ja konkreettista asiakastyötä.

- Aiemmin ilmoitetut kriteerit saavat nyt voimakkaamman oikeudellisen selkänojan, koska niiden periaatteet on yleistasolla kirjattu myöskin asetuksen tasolle, Rydman kertoi toimittajille valtioneuvoston istunnon jälkeen.

Asetusmuutos valmisteltiin pääministeri Petteri Orpon (kok.) vaatimuksesta sen jälkeen, kun Rydmanin linjaamista avustusten myöntämiskriteereistä repesi riita hallituksen sisällä aiemmin kesällä.

Nyt Rydman kommentoi, että kriteerit eivät ole oikeudellisesti eivätkä poliittisesti sitovia vaan virkamiesvalmistelun ohjeita. Hän sanoi, ettei järjestöille aiemmin annettua hakuilmoitusta ole tarvetta päivittää.

title: Tracking My Son to His Grave: Nina’s Story
content:
There are two remarkable things about the Ukrainian war documentary Peace for Nina, now touring the film festival circuit.

The first is the story it tells.

Ukrainian soldier Ihor Branovytsky was captured by Russian separatists when they overran Donetsk airport in 2014. After that, he vanished. The film follows his mother Nina’s search as she tracks down fellow prisoners who recount the horrible truth that Ihor was executed by a paramilitary leader and former car wash employee, Arsen Pavlov, nicknamed Motorola.

Remarkably, as news of her quest spread, a Kyiv journalist tracked down Motorola’s cellphone number. More remarkable still, Motorola gave an interview from across the front line. He wouldn’t comment on Branovytsky’s death, but blithely took credit for executing 15 other prisoners. A year after that, Motorola was himself dead, blown up by a bomb planted in the elevator of his apartment block by an unknown assassin.

title: I spent 18 months testing the best video doorbells – here are my favourites
content:
Whether you want to improve your home’s security or simply know who’s at the door, the latest generation of smart doorbells will help put your mind at ease

Doorbells have evolved. Today, they watch us as we approach, let the people inside the home know we’re coming sooner than our finger can hit the button, and give them a good look at our faces before they open the door. They’re essentially security cameras with a chime function.

Choosing the best video doorbell can be a bewildering task, with various factors to consider, including how much of your doorstep you want to see and whether you’re prepared to pay for a subscription. To help make the decision a little bit easier, I tested 11 popular video doorbells to find the best.

title: Afghanistan: Taliban Forcibly Disappear 6 Rights Workers
content:
(New York, August 12, 2026) – Taliban authorities in Afghanistan have forcibly disappeared six staff members of the nongovernmental group Women and Children Legal Research Foundation (WCLRF) for nearly a month, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Taliban have provided no information on the whereabouts of the organization’s leadership team, who were arrested in Kabul on July 18, 2026. The Women and Children Legal Research Foundation delivers assistance programs and conducts research and advocacy on women and children’s rights. The Taliban authorities should permit family members and legal counsel to visit those detained, and they should be immediately released unless they have been charged with a recognizable offense. 

“The Taliban seems to consider any effort to assist women and girls a threat to their abusive rule,” said Macarena Sáez, women’s rights director at Human Rights Watch. “They should immediately provide information on the six staff members’ whereabouts and release them if held unlawfully.”

title: Why does it feel like the US and Iran are stuck in an endless conflict loop?
content:
If you feel a sense of déjà vu with the state of the US–Iran war, you’re not alone.

In recent days, Iran has again demanded the Trump administration lift sanctions on the country, unfreeze Iranian assets and remove its military blockade, in return for Iran opening the Strait of Hormuz. This basically reiterates what the two sides agreed to in a memorandum of understanding in June.

US President Donald Trump responded by demanding Iran pay compensation for thousands of US soldiers and Iran’s own civilians killed over the past 50 years.

He is also claiming (again) the US has “total control” over the Strait of Hormuz, while Iran maintains the strait will remain closed until the US has met its conditions.

With both sides stuck in a rinse-and-repeat cycle in their rhetoric, it seems all the more likely they will again resort to military strikes to try to force the other side to concede. This has been the pattern both have followed since the war began on February 28.

Can this pattern ever be broken, and what would it take?

title: Vasemmistoliiton Kivelä: Peltokangas ei ole sopiva hallintovaliokunnan puheenjohtajaksi
content:
Kansanedustaja Mai Kivelän (vas.) mielestä kansanedustaja Mauri Peltokankaan (ps.) ala-arvoisten kommenttien täytyy johtaa eroon hallintovaliokunnan puheenjohtajan paikalta.

Kivelä kuvaa Peltokankaan taannoista Facebook-päivitystä avoimen rasistiseksi. Hän pitää selvänä, että Peltokangas viittaa siinä SDP:n varapuheenjohtajaan, kansanedustaja Nasima Razmyariin.

– On äärimmäisen vakava asia, että tällaista rasistista kielenkäyttöä suvaitaan suomalaisen päätöksenteon huipulla ja siten normalisoidaan osaksi yhteiskunnallista keskustelua, Kivelä sanoo tiedotteessa.

– Tämä ei ole ensimmäinen eikä viimeinen kerta, kun perussuomalaisilta tulee ala-arvoisia kirjoituksia ja tarkoituksella luotuja rasismikohuja. Perussuomalaiset elää ja hengittää rasismia, ja silti kokoomus on katsonut ja yhä katsoo hallitusyhteistyön hyväksi ideaksi.

Kivelän mukaan on erityisen vakavaa, että rasistisia kommentteja esittää hallintovaliokunnan puheenjohtaja. Hän muistuttaa, että valiokunta käsittelee paitsi ulkomaalaislainsäädäntöä, myös esimerkiksi poliisin toimivaltuuksia, jotka puuttuvat voimakkaasti muun muassa kansalaisten perusoikeuksiin.

title: Investing $4.9 million of our surplus in rebuilding the Crossref system - Crossref
content:
"The infrastructure that registers and distributes Crossref metadata has been running and growing for more than two decades. It now does considerably more than it was built to do, and it shows: two large, tightly coupled monoliths (Content System and REST API), where a change in one place risks breaking something in another.

In its July meeting, the Crossref board approved the use of Crossref surplus funds for a three-year project to accelerate the redesign of the Crossref system. Our plan is to use $1.6 million a year for three years (~USD $4.9M in total) from our surplus funds, which will help us set up a modern infrastructure consisting of separate services for the different functionalities that the Crossref system offers."

content:

Samsung’s top folding phone for 2026 is its first to carry the “Ultra” moniker in its name, packing a much bigger battery and better cameras into the thin and light body of a book-style foldable.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra continues from where the exquisite Z Fold 7 left off last year. With its svelte chocolate bar dimensions opening into a square tablet, the Ultra sits above the new passport-shaped Z Fold 8 as Samsung’s top model. Costing £1,899 (€2,199/$2,099.99/A$2,999), it is a lot of money to pay for a phone, regardless of how many other devices it can theoretically replace in your pocket.

title: US: Federal Agencies Abandon Civil Rights Duties
content:
(Washington, DC) – The Trump administration has gutted federal civil rights enforcement in the United States, leaving the people the laws were built to protect without adequate remedies, Human Rights Watch said in a report released today. 

The 112-page report, “Remedies Abandoned: US Civil Rights Enforcement Under the Trump Administration,” documents the administration’s efforts to unravel the work of four key agencies between January 2025 and the spring of 2026: the Justice Department’s Civil Rights Division, which lost about 75 percent of its attorneys; the Education Department’s Office of Civil Rights, which moved to lay off nearly half its staff in one day and closed 7 of its 12 regional offices; the Housing and Urban Development Department’s Fair Housing Office, which shrank dramatically; and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission, which reached its lowest staffing levels in over 40 years.

content:
Niin kutsuttua Tiitisen listaa ovat viime vuoden lopussa tai tämän vuoden alussa pyytäneet suojelupoliisilta (supo) käyttöönsä kolme tutkijaa sekä yksi tutkimusryhmä. Asiasta uutisoi Uutissuomalainen torstaina.

Uutissuomalaisen supolta saamien tietojen mukaan listaa pyytäneen tutkimusryhmän jäsenten joukossa ovat muun muassa emeritusprofessori Alpo Rusi ja toimittaja Pekka Virkki. Yhden listaa pyytäneen tutkijan nimeä supo ei anna julkisuuteen.

Supo ei ole toistaiseksi vastannut tutkimuspyyntöihin. Supon mukaan hakemusten käsittelyaika on noin 6-12 kuukautta.

Tiitisen listalla tarkoitetaan suojelupoliisin silloisen päällikön Seppo Tiitisen vuonna 1990 saamaa listaa 18 suomalaisesta, joilla on epäilty olleen yhteys Itä-Saksan tiedustelupalveluun Stasiin.

Supo epäili Alpo Rusia aikoinaan törkeästä vakoilusta entisen Itä-Saksan tiedustelupalvelun hyväksi, ja tieto esitutkinnasta valui julkisuuteen. Epäilyt eivät johtaneet syytteeseen, ja valtio tuomittiin maksamaan Rusille korvauksia.

title: The AI Era Arcs Toward Openness
content:
A surge of openness in AI has defined 2026. Amid calls for both caution and support, prevailing trends point to a future in which models are built and released openly. Recent research offers new insight into the adoption of open AI systems, who benefits, and the role of Open Source across the AI technology stack. The success of open-weight and Open Source AI reflects growing adoption, lower costs, narrowing performance gaps, and a desire for greater control over how AI is designed and implemented.

Recent reports document a considerable increase in the number of open AI projects on popular platforms such as GitHub, Hugging Face, and OpenRouter. The scale of AI development on public platforms is striking, even if public availability does not necessarily imply meaningful openness. Data from the 2026 Stanford AI Index Report shows that over 5 million AI-related projects were available on GitHub as of late 2025, up from a million in 2020. Similarly, the number of models available on HuggingFace has grown to over two million. This upward trend is likely to continue, seeing vocal calls in support of Open Source by a growing number of governments and organizations.

title: Maria Huhmarniemi kuvataidekasvatuksen professoriksi
content:
Dosentti, taiteen tohtori Maria Huhmarniemi on aloittanut kuvataidekasvatuksen professorina Lapin yliopiston taiteiden tiedekunnassa kesäkuun puolivälissä.

Kuvataidekasvatuksen tieteenalaan kuuluu keskeisesti kuvataideopettajakoulutus. Suomessa kuvataideopettajien koulutusta järjestetään Lapin yliopistossa ja Aalto-yliopistossa.

– Kuvataidekasvatuksen kenttä on laaja: se ulottuu peruskouluista lukioihin, ammatillisiin oppilaitoksiin ja taiteilijakoulutukseen. Alaa kehitetään ja tutkitaan myös taideperustaisissa palveluissa sekä virallisen koulujärjestelmän ulkopuolisissa ja arkielämän oppimistilanteissa, Maria Huhmarniemi kertoo.

Huhmarniemen professuurin painopisteenä on soveltava taide: erityisesti taiteen yhteiskunnallinen vaikuttavuus, kestävyysmurros sekä taiteen tekemisen ja kokemisen kasvatuksellinen merkitys. Hänen monitieteinen ja tulevaisuusorientoitunut tutkimuksensa keskittyy toimintaan, joka tukee kestävää kulttuuria ja kulttuurista kestävyysmurrosta.

title: Virolais-suomalainen Comand-hanke luo pohjaa paikallismuseoiden yhteistyölle
content:
Suomen Kotiseutuliitto on yhteistyökumppanina nyt loppukesällä alkavassa virolais-suomalaisessa Comand-hankkeessa. Hanke keskittyy erityisesti Peipsijärven alueen sekä eteläisen ja keskisen Suomen paikallismuseoihin. Tavoitteena on vahvistaa museoiden digitaalista osaamista sekä tehdä niistä saavutettavampia paikallisille yhteisöille, kouluille ja vierailijoille.

Comand – Museoesinekokoelmien digitointi verkostoyhteistyössä (Collections of Museum Artifacts for Networked Digitalization) -hanketta johtaa Peipsi Koostöö Keskus, englanninkieliseltä nimeltään Peipsi Cooperation Centre. Hanketta rahoittaa Central Baltic -ohjelma 2021–2027.

Hankkeeseen osallistuu neljä suomalaista paikallismuseota: Askolan kotiseutumuseo, Virtain Perinnekylä, Pernajan museo sekä Weteraanimoottorikerho Wanha Woima ja perinnekeskus. Virolaiset yhteistyömuseot sijaitsevat Peipsimaalla Peipsijärven seudulla. Virosta hankkeessa mukana olevat paikallismuseot ovat Peipsimaa Museum, Kalevipoja Koda, Liivi Museum, Iisaku Museum ja Kodavere Heritage Centre.

title: Kulttuurihyvinvoinnin ABC julkaistu – ota kulttuurihyvinvoinnin ammattisanasto eli jargon haltuun
content:
Tuore kulttuurihyvinvoinnin oppimateriaali Kulttuurihyvinvoinnin ABC – ableismista yleisötyöhön on erinomainen käsikirja kaikille kulttuuri- ja taidealan ammattilaisille, joiden täytyy osana työtään kertoa kulttuurin ja taiteen hyvinvointi- ja terveysvaikutuksista tai miettiä, miten omalta osaltaan saisi levitettyä näitä vaikutuksia laajemmalla joukolle suomalaisia. 

Julkaisun sydän on sanasto, joka sisältää toista sataa ammattilaisten käyttämää termiä. Se siis auttamaan käyttämään jargonia, joka on tarpeellista osata asioidessa sote- ja kulttuuripalvelujen rajapinnassa. Anteeksi, oikea termi on tietysti yhdyspinta. Tämän opin työskennellässäni kulttuurialan edustajana sote-uudistuksen yhdyspintatyöryhmässä.

Jargonille on helppo naureskella, mutta oikeasti se antaa työkalut poikkihallinnolliselle yhteistyölle, joka aina vaatii yhteistä kieltä. 

Kulttuurihyvinvoinnin ABC:n sanasto toimii kätevästi samalla hakemistona, joka auttaa löytämään kulttuurihyvinvoinnin tietoperustan ja moninaiset lähestymistavat. Ovathan kysymykset toiset, pohtiiko asiaa lastensuojelun työntekijän, vanhuspalvelujen suunnittelijan tai soveltavasta taiteesta kiinnostuneen taiteilijan näkökulmasta.

title: Inventing Telephones at the 1876 Centennial
content:
-This is a guest post by Josh Levy, a historian in the Manuscript Division. It also appears in the May/June issue of the Library of Congress Magazine.

In June of 1876, two weeks before the nation’s centennial, a young Alexander Graham Bell arrived in Philadelphia. He was staggered by what he saw. He had come to demonstrate his inventions at the Centennial Exposition, the first world’s fair hosted on American soil, with exhibits stretched massively across more than 200 buildings in Fairmount Park. “It grows upon one,” Bell wrote his soon-to-be wife, Mabel. “It is so prodigious and so wonderful … just think of having the products of all nations condensed into a few acres of buildings.”

Like any of the era’s world’s fairs, the exhibition was a breathless celebration of progress, a spectacle of industry and commerce, art and culture. Nearly 10 million visitors attended. Those visitors may easily have passed by Bell’s telephone, but the impression of the nation’s burgeoning industrial power was unmistakable.

title: The Most Controversial Ancient Philosophy: Epicureanism
content:
Over the years, you’ve probably heard at least a few people casually describe themselves as Epicureans. As used today, the label can refer to as little as enjoying the occasional expensive restaurant meal. The bar was a bit higher in the second century, as explained by ancient-history YouTuber Garrett Ryan in the new video above from his channel Told in Stone. But there is, at least, one major aspect of the original doctrine laid out by Epicurus (341–270 BC) with which most any of his self-styled followers in our time would agree: that pleasure is the greatest good. Whether they would follow that premise all the way to the conclusions Epicurus did is another matter.

For that ancient Greek philosopher, Ryan explains, “happiness was the sole legitimate goal of human existence. The essence of happiness is freedom from anxiety. Since the greatest source of mental disturbance is fear about death and the afterlife, it is necessary to understand the true nature of the universe.”

title: Announcing Four Regional Events for CC’s 25th Anniversary
content:
We are excited to announce that we will be supporting four regional events for CC’s 25th Anniversary—representing regions around the world with groups who are working to advance open knowledge. We’re delighted to be working with a variety of trusted partners and look forward to sharing more about their plans and reporting back on how these events went. 

We want to thank everyone who submitted a proposal for an event. There were so many great ideas, and we hope to have more opportunities to support regional work like this in the future. 

In Córdoba, LibreBase will celebrate 25 years of Creative Commons alongside Argentina’s longstanding cultura libre, free software, and open knowledge communities. The one-day gathering will bring together creators, educators, researchers, publishers, technologists, and activists for conversations and hands-on workshops exploring the impact of open licensing across culture, education, and knowledge. Participants can explore a showcase and digital swap of CC-licensed works, learn about remixing and Wikimedia Commons, and join a closing conversation on the future of the digital commons including emerging questions around generative AI.

title: BMW’s in-car Spider-Man ad is a warning sign
content:
I don’t know about you, but the one thing I’ve always though was missing from the driving experience was having a car I paid tens of thousands of dollars for start blasting me with ads now that it’s always connected to the internet. It wasn’t enough that there are billboards littered all around the roads we drive on for companies to try to capture our attention. I’ve always wanted them plastered on the increasingly large screen in my center console.

I am, of course, being sarcastic. But we recently saw one of the inevitable developments from the “connected car” that automakers (and tech companies) have been pushing us toward for more than a decade. Starting on July 27, when BMW owners turned on their vehicles they were met with a special surprise: an exclusive ad for the new Spider-Man: Brand New Day movie.

title: Trump sued over paid early access to Truth Social posts
content:
A news organization and free speech nonprofit sued President Donald Trump over his social media platform’s program that offers paid early access to his posts after the scheme went live at the beginning of August.

The lawsuit, filed Wednesday in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York by the left-leaning nonprofit newsroom The Intercept and the Freedom of the Press Foundation, alleges the practice “is extraordinary, corrupt, and unconstitutional.”

The plaintiffs also say the controversial $100,000-a-month program violates their First Amendment rights to access presidential statements “on equal terms with other members of the press and public.”

In announcing plans to introduce the program, Truth Social — whose parent company Trump founded in 2021 after being kicked off social media platforms and owns a plurality stake in — described the initiative as valuable for “organizations that place a premium on immediate, verified access to information.” But critics allege it amounts to insider trading on advanced access to the president’s market-moving words.

title: Humanitaarisiin työntekijöihin kohdistuvat hyökkäykset ennätystasolla – droonit vaikeuttavat avun perillepääsyä
content:
Yli tuhat humanitaarista työntekijää on kuollut viimeisen kolmen vuoden aikana, ja konfliktialueilla yleistyneet droonit vaikeuttavat entisestään avun toimittamista lapsille ja perheille.

Vuonna 2025 kuoli 350 humanitaarista työntekijää, mikä on toiseksi suurin koskaan kirjattu määrä.

Droonit ja muu uusi sotateknologia sulkevat teitä, keskeyttävät avustusoperaatioita ja estävät avustustyöntekijöitä toimittamasta apua perille. Lisäksi hyökkäykset kohdistuvat yhä useammin sairaaloihin, terveydenhuoltoon ja kouluihin.

- Avun on päästävä perille ja siviilejä on suojeltava. Meidän on varmistettava, että avustustyöntekijöitä, sairaaloita ja muuta siviili-infrastruktuuria vastaan tehdyistä hyökkäyksistä joutuu vastuuseen, World Vision Nordicin toiminnanjohtaja Annette Gothóni sanoo.

- Kun avustustyöntekijöitä kohti hyökätään, lapset jäävät ilman ruokaa, lääkkeitä ja muuta elintärkeää hätäapua. Turvallisuusuhat vaikeuttavat avustustyötä ja voivat edesauttaa nälänhädän kehittymistä ja muuta inhimillistä kärsimystä.

Humanitaarisen avun päivänä 19.8.2026 kunnioitetaan avustustyötä tekeviä sekä sen parissa menehtyneitä.

title: What it is like to run a business as a woman in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan
content:
No area of women's lives is safe from the Taliban restrictions

Originally published on Global Voices

Women in Afghanistan. Screenshot from the video ‘Women’s rights being rolled back in Afghanistan – BBC News’ on the BBC News YouTube channel. Fair use.

This article was written by Arezo in 2025. It is being published with her consent as part of a special coverage series that tells the stories of young women and girls from Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover in August 2021.

Since the occupation of Afghanistan in August 2021, the Taliban has been actively violating people’s human rights and dismantling the structures that protect them. This is especially true for women and girls, as the Taliban has imposed strict laws that have practically destroyed their basic rights and freedoms.

Among these laws was the closure of schools, universities, and educational centers for women and girls. Another is the ban on women working in the government and private sectors. This removal of women from the economic and public sphere is one of the greatest injustices and oppressions that have been committed against Afghan women.

title: Choosing Courage over Despair: Civil Society Is Notching Up Wins Despite Hostile Conditions
content:
By Mandeep Tiwana, CIVICUS Secretary General

We live in a world where cruel and unaccountable power is on the ascendant. Powerful countries led by self-serving strongmen are wreaking havoc across borders in a neocolonial scramble for power and natural resources. Their disruption of the rules-based order through military action in breach of international law is leaving trails of death and destruction. Oligarchs powered by the entrenchment of market fundamentalism have come to monopolize large swaths of our economies. They are trying to influence how people think and act through their grip on the media, boosted by artificial intelligence (AI) and surveillance technology. These combined forces want civil society to believe nothing can stand in their way. But across the world, despite immensely challenging conditions, resistance is brewing and is notching up wins for peace, justice, equality, and environmental sustainability.

title: When Disinformation Takes to the Streets and Causes Harm
content:
Six men and one woman have been remanded in custody for 30 days over an attack on an ambulance in a village in Cluj County, with the woman facing assault charges. Prosecutors said she threw a stone at the ambulance window, injuring the driver.

On Monday morning, the ambulance driver underwent a second surgery after sustaining an eye injury from shards of the shattered window.

The seven suspects stormed an ambulance with clubs, axes and stones after believing false information that had appeared on TikTok. The ambulance had picked up a patient and was taking them to hospital when it was attacked. The viral video invoked the myth of “black ambulances” – a conspiracy theory that has circulated in Romania in the past – which allegedly kidnap children.

Police identified those involved in the incident, which took place on August 8. They are aged between 18 and 44 and come from a village in western Romania.

title: Paper Tiger: The Failure of America’s Trillion Dollar War Machine
content:
By Medea Benjamin and Nicolas J. S. Davies*

NEW YORK | 13 August 2026 (IDN) — According to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), the United States spent $21 trillion on its military between 2001 and 2024 (in constant 2024 dollars), equal to the combined military spending of the next eighteen countries. Iran barely made that list at all, spending only 2% of what the US did, and SIPRI estimated Iran’s 2025 military budget at only $7.5 billion. So how is Iran holding its own against the multi-trillion-dollar US war machine?

A critical difference between the US war on Iran and previous US and allied bombing campaigns against Yugoslavia, Afghanistan, Iraq, Libya and now Gaza is that the US and Israel have failed to destroy Iran’s air defence system and cannot fly warplanes over Iran without risking the loss of planes and pilots to enemy fire. Iran has wisely built its critical defence infrastructure underground, with arms factories, weapons stockpiles and launch sites sheltered safely beneath its impenetrable mountainous terrain.

title: Dutch Court Hears Case against Whistleblower’s Murder Suspect
content:
Just five days before a whistleblower who exposed a sprawling illegal gambling network was gunned down in the Netherlands, police briefly detained a key suspect in the killing after intercepting him in a car packed with weapons and bearing stolen licence plates, a Dutch court heard on Wednesday.

Cemil Önal had warned authorities for weeks that his life was in danger after he leaked details of what he claimed was a multi-million-dollar bribery ring linking organized crime to Turkish public officials.

Nevertheless, the former finance director for Turkish Cypriot casino kingpin Halil Falyalı, was gunned down on a hotel terrace in the town of Rijswijk, Netherlands in May 2025. 

The suspect, Hasan Y., a 31-year-old Turkish national, was stopped by police on April 25 in the town of Barneveld in a vehicle with stolen plates. Officers impounded the car but released Hasan Y. It was only after his release that investigators searched the vehicle thoroughly and discovered a Glock pistol and ammunition inside.

By the time police realized what was in the car, it was too late. On a hotel terrace in the Dutch town of Rijswijk, Önal was shot dead.

title: Fiasco in the Factory: Taxpayers Funded a $533 Million Artillery Plant That Made Nothing
content:
A robot was on fire. Again.

It was the summer of 2024, and the cutting-edge robots inside General Dynamics’ sweltering artillery factory near Dallas were catching fire with startling regularity, according to four former workers there. This wasn’t ideal, as the plant was supposed to be churning out urgently needed artillery shells for Ukraine. The robots, giant metal arms with clamps for hands, would end up drenched in oil, which would then — no surprise — combust as they moved steel blocks heated to 1,800 degrees into and out of a machine that periodically erupted columns of fire. One blaze that summer melted a robot’s cables, putting it out of commission for a week.

Only weeks earlier, defense officials and executives had touted the factory’s innovative new machinery, imported from Turkey, at a gala opening ceremony. But employees were already used to spectacular mishaps, fiery and otherwise. “After the second, third, fourth time, it just became almost normal,” one former worker said. “It got to the point where I was not surprised by anything that happened there.”

title: Marokkolainen aavikkoleiri saa miettimään omaa identiteettiä
content:
Kuka on muukalainen aavikolla – matkailija vai ihminen, jolla on alueella vuosituhansien mittaiset juuret? Ja läheinen suhde kameleihin, noihin aavikoiden laivoihin?

”Habibi! Habibi!” Kamelinomistaja toistelee puolisolleni arabiankielistä sanaa. Opimme, että sana tarkoittaa ystävää. Naiselle lausuttuna se taipuisi muotoon habibti.

Kun yhteistä kieltä ei ole, kielimuurista tulee huomaamatta ystävyyden rakentaja. Ja mikä olisikaan parempi sana rakentamaan siltaa ventovieraiden välille? ”Ystävä.” Nyökkäys. ”Ystävä.”

Olemme tulleet yöksi Agafayn aavikkoleiriin kivenheiton päässä Marrakechista. Totuus on, että kyseisen miehen parhaita ystäviä eivät suinkaan ole kaltaisemme muukalaiset vaan edessämme leukojaan louskuttelevat kamelit.

Kamelit ja amazighit – joita kutsutaan myös berbereiksi – ovat olleet erottamattomia jo vuosisatojen ajan. Matkailijoille tämä yhteys välittyy esimerkiksi kameliretkillä, joilla oppaat tuovat esille ”aavikkonomadeinakin” tunnetun kansan ja ”aavikkolaivoiksikin” kutsuttujen eläinten välistä kumppanuutta.

On jopa sanottu, että amazighien ja arabien välinen suhde muodostaa perustan koko modernille marokkolaiselle identiteetille.

title: What it’s like to discover an ancient Egyptian tomb – and the race against time to preserve it
content:
The first moment you look inside a newly discovered ancient tomb is at once exciting and terrifying. I was fortunate to experience this recently as director of an international research team carrying out fieldwork in the Theban necropolis, a Unesco world heritage site near the modern Egyptian city of Luxor.

Our project’s primary aim is to implement a conservation and risk management programme for the necropolis (burial ground) of Lower Sheikh ʿAbd el-Qurna. Due to its location at the foothills of the Theban mountain, monuments in this area are extremely vulnerable to flash flooding from intense bursts of rain.

To direct this floodwater away from the tombs, we are systematically removing debris and excavating the area, using archaeological techniques that ensure all historical information is preserved. This is how we came across this previously unknown, roughly 3,000-year-old tomb.

As we prepared to enter it, we had no idea if the ceiling had collapsed, if the tomb had been looted or destroyed, or if it was still well preserved.

title: Analysis: Weaker EV targets could cost UK consumers £3bn a year by 2030
content:
An upcoming UK government consultation on weakening targets for electric vehicles (EVs) could cost consumers as much as £3bn a year by 2030, according to Carbon Brief analysis.

It could require the UK to import an extra 17m barrels of oil in 2030, raising expected net imports by 8%, as well as adding 2.5% to national emissions that year, the analysis shows.

After years of fierce lobbying by parts of the car industry – and despite the significant savings on offer for EV drivers – media reports suggest that EV targets could be “watered down”.

Under current rules, battery EVs – BEVs, those which run only on electricity – must make up a rising share of new car sales in the UK.

This policy, known as the “zero-emission vehicles” (ZEV) mandate, was introduced by the previous Conservative government and sets a goal for 33% BEV sales in 2026, rising to 80% in 2030.

(Carmakers are able to use “flexibilities” to help meet their targets, which reduces the effective target under the ZEV mandate to an estimated 25% of sales in 2026.)

title: Ukrainian Justice Struggles to Keep Pace with Russia’s Crimes
content:
Ukraine’s war crimes investigation and prosecution system has matured substantially since 2022, with specialized war crimes departments now embedded across the Office of the Prosecutor General (OPG), regional prosecutors’ offices, the Security Service, and the National Police.

Independent reviewers, including the War Crimes Trial Monitoring Initiative, have reported that the justice process is broadly effective. But it faces structural and legal constraints that threaten to undermine its efficiency as the number of cases grows.

The most acute structural gap is capacity. By June 2026, more than 240,000 episodes had been recorded in the Unified Register of Pre-Trial Investigations in Ukraine, a volume of cases few investigative or prosecutorial bodies could reasonably process.

While the number of episodes will not necessarily equal the number of prosecutions, as some will be merged due to common perpetrators, the means used, or the targeted territory, it is still a titanic workload.

title: Not All Research Environments are Created Equal: Structural Injustice in Low-Resourced Scientific Settings and Its Epistemic Implications
content: Abstract: This paper discusses three forms of structural injustice associated with disparities in the resources available to researchers, and the opportunity researchers have to pursue their scientific goals. These are: (1) resource injustice; (2) focus injustice; and (3) labour injustice. I argue that such structural injustice has significant epistemic implications, resulting in: shifts in research content; the exclusion of substantive portions of scientific community from contributing to knowledge production to the best of their abilities; the exclusion of specific methods and data sources from global scientific discourse, on grounds other than scientific quality and relevance; a loss of quality and reliability in processes and outcomes of inquiry; and the inability to implement openness and related forms of constructive scrutiny. To exemplify these forms of injustice and their epistemic implications, I discuss everyday challenges within life science sites in Italy, Ghana and Greece, as documented through ethnographic research. I conclude that structural injustice permeates the institutional and material conditions for the acquisition and evaluation of knowledge in many research

title: Investigating Inside Conflict Zones and Areas Controlled by Armed Groups: Lessons from South Asia and the Middle East
content:
In October 2021, journalist Shahid Zehri was driving home to Karachi through the town of Hub, in Pakistan’s Balochistan province, when a bomb planted under his car seat detonated. He died of his injuries hours later.

The Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA), a separatist rebel group regarded as a terrorist organization by the Pakistani government and several other countries, including the United States, claimed responsibility, accusing Zehri of spying for Pakistan’s security forces, without offering evidence. “It is intolerable that separatist rebels are able, with impunity, to claim the right to kill journalists in a completely arbitrary manner,” Reporters Without Borders (RSF) spokesperson Pauline Adès-Mével said in a statement in response to the killing.

title: Watch Stewart Brand’s 6‑Part Series How Buildings Learn, With Music by Brian Eno
content:
Stewart Brand came onto the cultural scene during the 1960s, helping to stage the Acid Tests made famous by Ken Kesey and the Merry Pranksters, and later launching the influential Whole Earth Catalog (something Steve Jobs described as “Google in paperback form, 35 years before Google came along”). He also vigorously campaigned in 1966 to have NASA release a photograph showing the entirety of Earth from space—something we take for granted now, but fired humanity’s imagination back then.

During the 1970s and beyond, Brand founded CoEvolution Quarterly, a successor to the Whole Earth Catalog; the WELL (“Whole Earth ‘Lectronic Link”), “a prototypical, wide-ranging online community for intelligent, informed participants the world over;” and eventually The Long Now Foundation, whose work we’ve highlighted here before. When not creating new institutions, he has poured his creative energies into books and films.

title: Poland rekindles Musk feud over Starlink snub
content:
Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski on Wednesday threatened to reconsider Warsaw’s $50 million-a-year spending on Elon Musk’s Starlink network, joining a growing government backlash over new roaming restrictions set to hit Polish customers later this month.

“Hey, @elonmusk, big man, stop discriminating Polish users of Starlink or we might re-think paying you $50 million p.a. for your services,” wrote Sikorski on X.

The foreign minister’s anger follows Starlink’s decision to exclude Poland from a shared European roaming zone that covers more than 30 countries, including Germany, Czechia, Slovakia and Lithuania. Customers within the zone can take their terminals across borders without triggering international-use restrictions. But Polish users will now face extra requirements when traveling.

“Note: Poland is not included in the Europe region above. Accounts registered in Poland are treated as Poland-only for home-country use,” reads Starlink’s current guidance.

Polish Digital Affairs Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski also went after Musk, accusing Starlink’s parent company SpaceX of treating Poles as second-class customers and demanding it spell out the regulatory basis for the change.

title: After 30 years of cultural revival, the Siraya reclaim their Indigenous status in Taiwan
content:
It has taken more than 30 years for the Siraya to rediscover and revive their language and culture

Originally published on Global Voices

Siraya activist Cheng-hiong Talavan led the younger generation in singing an ancient Siraya song. Screenshot from Onini315‘s YouTube channel

This post is part of Global Voices’ August 2026 Spotlight series, “Indigenous Rights.” This series offers insight into the lives and experiences of Indigenous peoples to build connections across regions, center Indigenous experiences, and share the stories of leaders, activists, community members, and more. You can support this coverage by donating here.

Indigenous Siraya were officially recognized via executive decree as Taiwan’s 17th indigenous group on July 30. They are also the first plains tribe group to obtain Indigenous status after the passage of the Plains Indigenous Peoples Status Act in October 2025. 

Like other Indigenous tribes in Taiwan, Siraya society was matriarchal, and its people, belonging to the Austronesian, spoke a distinctive language known as Sinckan, which was recorded through romanization by missionaries during the Dutch colonial era (1624–1662).

title: Art, Surveillance and the Politics of Memory
content:
By Deepthy Menon, Strategy and Narratives Facilitator, Urgent Action Fund Asia and Pacific

Across Southeast Asia, artists and cultural rights defenders are increasingly being cast as threats – to public morality, political order and dominant narratives about gender, sexuality, identity and belonging.

This is especially true for queer and trans artists, whose bodies, stories and performances often challenge the boundaries that states, religious authorities and conservative movements seek to impose. When their work is censored, surveilled or attacked, the consequences reach beyond artistic freedom. They touch the foundations of civic space: the right to speak, gather, remember, imagine and contest power.

Read more on The Diplomat

title: Mark Rutte and the Trump gamble: Saving NATO at what cost?
content:
Since taking over as NATO secretary general, the former Dutch prime minister has cultivated a remarkably warm relationship with Donald Trump. He praises him publicly, credits him with achievements that began long before his return to the White House and rarely challenges him in front of the cameras.

The strategy has produced results. Trump remains engaged with NATO. The alliance has agreed to a dramatic increase in defence spending. And the American president has repeatedly praised Rutte himself.

But there is an increasingly uncomfortable question in European capitals: when does strategic flattery become strategic dependence?

Mark Rutte’s supporters argue that he is doing exactly what the alliance needs in an exceptionally dangerous period. His critics fear that, in trying to keep Trump inside NATO, he may be weakening the very institution he is supposed to lead.

The NATO secretary general is not a commander-in-chief. He does not decide where American troops are deployed, nor can he order European governments to spend more on defence. His principal power is political: persuasion, mediation and consensus-building.

title: Thailand and Myanmar Sign Agreement To Tackle Transboundary River Pollution, But Can They Do It Alone?
content:
By Kalinga Seneviratne*

BANGKOK, Thailand | 12 August 2026 (IDN) — Witnessed by the visiting Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing and Thailand’s Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, the two ASEAN members signed a Terms of Reference (TOR) on 7th August for the establishment of a joint working group on water quality management for transboundary rivers, such as the Sai and Kok rivers, which have been contaminated from unregulated rare earth mining activities in Myanmar’s Shan state, in areas that is controlled by several armed minority groups, such as United Wa State Army (UWSA).

The TOR was signed by Dr. Raweewan Bhuridej, Permanent Secretary of Thailand’s Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment and her counterpart, Hla Maung Thein, Permanent Secretary of Myanmar’s Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation.

Bhuridej told Thai PBS that while the agreement marks an important step forward in cooperation between the two countries in addressing the unresolved pollution problem that has been dragging on for 2 years, yet, she admitted, that there are obstacles to implementing the agreement because the Myanmar government is not in full control of the Shan State.

title: Twitch is Mining Peoples' Streams to Train Amazon's AI
content:
Twitch is going to train Amazon’s AI models on streamers’ content unless they deliberately go into their settings and opt out, potentially sweeping up a wealth of streamers who either don’t hear about the announcement or follow steps stop it.

On Wednesday Twitch announced a new setting that lets streamers opt-out of the training. The announcement confirms rumors that have percolated over the last week: It is using streamers to train Amazon’s AI models. 

The new toggle says, "Allow your channel content to train generative AI content models at Amazon." All users are opted in by default. It's located at the bottom of users' security settings page.

title: Treasury Rolls Back Ownership Reporting Obligations for U.S. Companies
content:
The U.S. Department of the Treasury has permanently eliminated beneficial ownership reporting requirements for domestic companies and individuals under the Corporate Transparency Act, gutting a major federal anti-money-laundering disclosure program for American small businesses.

The rule effectively exempts U.S. citizens operating domestic businesses from disclosing their beneficial ownership information as was mandated under the Corporate Transparency Act, a landmark anti-corruption law enacted in December 2020, aimed at combating money laundering and illicit finance.

Under the update, foreign companies must still report beneficial ownership information for foreign individuals to FinCEN. However, foreign companies are exempt from reporting ownership information regarding U.S. citizens, as well as details about Americans who assist them in registering to conduct business within the U.S.

FinCEN also announced that it will delete all previously collected information regarding U.S. business owners from its beneficial ownership database.

title: “They’re Putting Kids’ Lives at Risk”: How Abuse in a Tennessee Businessman’s Juvenile Prisons Remained Under Wraps
content:
The video clip lasted less than two minutes, but Tonya Webb remembers every second as heartbreaking.

The grainy surveillance footage, dated June 29, 2024, showed a teenager in an anti-suicide smock being dragged violently by other teens across the floor at Middle Tennessee Juvenile Detention Center. As guards watched, the teens pulled the smock over the boy’s head, exposing his naked body. Then they stuffed him, limbs flailing, into a cell.

One guard pushed the door closed, locking him in, and the boy pressed his face against the sliver of a cell window. The guard flashed the teens a thumbs-up.

Webb, a medication supervisor at the facility, saw the video when a co-worker showed it to her and knew she was looking at a serious violation of state policy. An incident like this one, in which employees encouraged youths to restrain another youth, would require staff to notify both the state and the boy’s family within 24 hours.

Webb said she raised questions about the incident with the compliance director for the facility. The director said she’d handle it, but after weeks went by with no sign of a state investigation, Webb confronted the deputy to the facility’s executive director.
snippet: The video clip lasted less than two minutes, but Tonya Webb remembers every second as heartbreaking.

content: "But given the many different ways to connect in the Fediverse—why do almost all academic associations or institutions choose a Mastodon server, of all things, for their communities? title: Silencing Journalists Online: How Copyright Is Being Weaponized Against Investigative Journalists
content:
A new form of censorship is emerging globally to silence the work of journalists and activists. On digital platforms like Facebook or Google, journalists’ social media accounts and their stories are being targeted with fake complaints aimed at silencing their work online.

The perpetrators are often shady firms hired by powerful interests who offer to remove content their clients don’t like online by playing with digital platforms rules.

Reputation cleaning firms or individuals make up false claims of copyright infringement and pressure the digital platforms to take down targeted contents. Do they succeed? Often, they do.  And Big Tech companies sometimes even refuse to disclose information on who makes these complaints.

The mechanics are straightforward and hard to fight: scammers duplicate the journalists’ social media accounts or content and file fake copyright infringement claims to digital platforms, accusing the journalists of impersonating them thus violating the platforms’ rules. This results in the journalists’ accounts or posts being suspended or banned, with the victims sometimes not being aware of the reasons they’re kicked out.

title: AI was supposed to destroy jobs. Where’s the carnage?
content:
The AI jobs apocalypse never showed up. Still, jobs are changing and economists expect more to come

The prediction was stark: artificial intelligence advancements would wipe out jobs en masse. “Half” of all entry-level white collar jobs would vanish, Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, said in May 2025. A month later, OpenAI’s CEO, Sam Altman, went further, foreseeing the end of “certain job categories”. Companies began citing AI in their layoffs. Workers organized. And students reconsidered their future careers.

But a year later, the mass carnage hasn’t shown up.

title: Meta AI glasses face criminal complaint in Germany
content:
A Berlin-based non-profit has filed a criminal complaint against Meta’s smart glasses, arguing the devices breach Germany’s strict privacy rules and should be banned.

Privacy concerns over the device have snowballed in recent months amid reports of people being filmed without their consent, or recording intimate footage without knowing it could be reviewed by Meta contractors.

The non-profit HateAid is arguing that the sale of Meta smart glasses in Germany is a criminal offense because the devices allow wearers to covertly film other people.

The complaint, which alleges the sale breaches Germany’s Telecommunications, Digital Services and Data Protection Act, was filed against Meta, Ray-Ban and Oakley — eyewear brands that have partnered with Meta to design the glasses — and several retailers.

Meta spokesperson Matthew Pollard said the smart glasses were approved by Germany’s regulator BNetzA in 2022, and “were built with privacy safeguards from the ground up that go beyond what any smartphone offers.” Those include an LED light that turns on when the glasses are recording, as well as technology to stop anyone from tampering with the light.
snippet: A Berlin-based non-profit has filed a criminal complaint against Meta’s smart glasses, arguing the devices breach Germany’s strict privacy rules and should be banned.

title: EU unemployment remains stable, but 3 million young people are out of work
content:
The labor market and the specter of unemployment are topics that have kept both European governments and ordinary citizens awake at night for decades. Older observers certainly remember the tragic realities of 2013, when the unemployment rate across the European Union reached almost 12 percent, and among young people exceeded an alarming 25 percent. 

At the time, this meant that every fourth young European was unemployed. Somewhat fresher in our memory are the times of the COVID-19 pandemic, when mass lockdowns paralyzed the service sector, driving the unemployment rate in 2020 up to 7.8 percent, with a striking result of 19.2 percent among the youth.

Against the backdrop of these past shocks, today’s situation appears remarkably stable. According to the latest Eurostat data for June 2026, the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate stood at 6.3 percent in the euro area and exactly 6.0 percent across the European Union — unchanged from a year earlier. Although these figures may look reassuring, they still translate into more than 13.3 million unemployed people across the EU, including over 11 million in the euro area.

title: Iraq PM’s Anti-Corruption Campaign Rumbles On
content:
Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi signaled this week that all corrupt officials — no matter how powerful — would face justice, as his high profile anti-graft campaign saw arrest warrants issued for a particularly prominent former government minister. 

“There are no red lines in pursuing the corrupt... and we call on the ladies and gentlemen of parliament to exercise their oversight role in supporting the government's efforts to combat corruption and dry up its sources,” al-Zaidi posted on his Facebook page Tuesday. 

The premier made the comment after the state Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported on Sunday the Baghdad/Karkh Court of Appeal had issued two arrest and search warrants for former Minister of Labor and Social Affairs, Ahmed Jasim Saber al-Asadi.

Al-Asadi is a former spokesperson for a group of Iran-backed militias central to Iraq’s security apparatus and a leader in the Shiite political alliance that was key to forming the premier’s government. The charges against Al-Asadi allege unexplained enrichment and “awarding contracts in violation of the law to benefit himself and others,” the INA reported.

title: Open practices across science, software, education and other domains | Nature Human Behaviour
content: Abstract:  Open practices are actions people perform to influence transparency (who can see information), inclusion (who can voice perspectives) and decision rights (who can make decisions). Open practices have grown popular across domains, including open science, open-source software and open education, in hopes of spurring innovation and broadening participation. But which open practices best enable groups and organizations to achieve these ambitious goals, and why? This Perspective distils seven successful practices from across these domains that can help groups to define goals, allocate power, share information and set norms. These practices, such as documenting power structures and adopting a code of conduct, hold potential to support groups and organizations seeking to address great challenges through openness. However, delivering on that potential will depend on how well groups share lessons across domains, tailor these practices and sustain the people and platforms that carry them.

title: ‘Much faster than originally planned’: Ukraine warns of Russian rival to Musk’s Starlink
content:
KYIV — Russia is racing to build its own low-orbit satellite internet system that could leave Ukraine vulnerable to more attacks, the deputy chief of Ukraine’s military intelligence, Maj. Gen. Vadym Skibitskiy, warned this week.  

Ukraine gained an edge on the battlefield earlier this year after Elon Musk was persuaded by Ukraine’s former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov to cut off access for Russian forces operating in Ukraine. That complicated Russian communications and targeting.

Now Russia is racing to build Rassvet, or Dawn, an equivalent to SpaceX’s Starlink being developed by Russian aerospace company Bureau 1440.

“They have begun launching it much faster than originally planned,” said Skibitskiy.

Russia launched the first 16 satellites of Rassvet in March. Bureau 1440 reported the successful launch of a second package of satellites in July.

“The spacecraft separated from the launch vehicle and contacted the flight control center. After completion of checks and commissioning of the subsystems, the satellites will begin transition to the target orbit to provide communication services,” Bureau 1440 said.

title: Will Migrants from Ceuta Flood Europe? The Truth About the Spanish Government’s Decision
content:
Two days at the turn of July and August 2026 were enough for a storm to erupt across the European web, the likes of which the continent had not seen since the great migration crisis a decade ago. When about 60,000 migrants from Morocco attempted to illegally enter Ceuta – a Spanish exclave in North Africa – the internet was flooded with a wave of apocalyptic forecasts. 

According to the most popular narrative, repeated by politicians and anonymous internet users, the left-wing government in Madrid was supposed to welcome all newcomers with open arms, hand them European documents, and open the borders, allowing for an uncontrolled “spillover” of migrants across the entire Schengen area. The problem is that in this virtual scenario, almost nothing matches the facts.

By analyzing the events from the Iberian Peninsula and North Africa step by step, one can see how a coincidence of circumstances, complex laws, and the deliberate activities of smugglers created an ideal environment for disinformation. Here is how the alleged “invasion of Europe” looks when confronted with reality.

title: Researchers Show How Meta's 'Pervert Glasses' Are Used to Harass Women
content:
Instagram is full of first-person videos of men harassing women in public. They follow a similar script: A man walks up to a woman or group of women in a store, sitting outside a cafe, or walking home from a bar, and delivers a pickup line. The women almost always nervously laugh, react with barely-veiled disgust, or say "fuck off" while he stalks her or refuses to walk away. The men recording these videos capture them with Meta's smart glasses, which are designed to discreetly capture interactions like these and upload the videos to Meta's platforms where the women in the videos are turned into content for "pickup artist" accounts.  

New research reveals this ecosystem works, and how pickup artists (PUA) influencers are using Meta's products, including its smart glasses and social media platforms, to perpetuate a culture of harassment against women.

title: AI Generated 3D Models Flood Market, But Almost No One Is Buying Them
content:
CGTrader, an online marketplace for 3D assets, found that one in six models uploaded to the site these days is AI generated, but that AI generated assets account for only $1 out of $90 in revenue on the site. These numbers show that AI generated assets are quickly flooding the marketplace, but that most people are not interested in paying for them.

“Buyers are voting with their wallets, and AI-generated content is struggling to compete,” CGTrader said in a press release about its 2026 market trends reports. The company says the gap between the surging supply of AI generated 3D models and the middling demand points to “a gap that undercuts the assumption that AI-made content is repricing the market.”

“The upload numbers alone would suggest a takeover,” CGTrader said. “The revenue numbers say otherwise, and buyers refusing to pay for AI-generated models is saying something bigger than no thanks: it is a signal of how far they trust AI generation itself. Which leaves the question the industry has been avoiding: an AI model may be cheaper to produce, but what is it actually worth?”

title: „Wiki Loves“-Wettbewerbe: Das sind die preisgekrönten Bilder 2026
content:
Jahr für Jahr beteiligen sich Menschen auf der ganzen Welt an den „Wiki Loves“-Fotowettbewerben. Ob beeindruckende Architektur, schützenswerte Naturräume oder gelebte Traditionen – die eingereichten Aufnahmen dokumentieren die Vielfalt unseres kulturellen und Naturerbes. Das Engagement der Teilnehmenden leistet somit einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Bewahrung und Vermittlung von Wissen.

Die einzelnen Wettbewerbe setzen dabei unterschiedliche Schwerpunkte:

  • Wiki Loves Monuments konzentriert sich auf Kultur- und Baudenkmäler,
  • Wiki Loves Earth widmet sich den Naturlandschaften und Schutzgebieten,
  • Wiki Loves Folklore rückt wiederum Bräuche, Feste und kulturelle Traditionen ins Bild.

title: Ulla Hemminki-Reijonen Funidatan uudeksi johtajaksi
content:
Ulla Hemminki-Reijonen aloittaa tehtävässään 17.8.2026 ja toimii Funidatan johtoryhmän jäsenenä.

"Funidatan kasvun kannalta kaksi asiaa ratkaisee: kuinka nopeasti saamme tekoälyn tuomat mahdollisuudet osaksi tuotteidemme toiminnallisuutta ja kuinka skaalautuvasti pystymme viemään järjestelmät korkeakoulujen käyttöön. Siksi kokosimme tuotehallinnan ja projektitoimitusten johtamisen saman vastuun alle. Ulla Hemminki-Reijosella on tähän harvinaisen vahva yhdistelmä: tuotejohtamisen kokemus, tekoälyosaaminen ja korkeakoulukentän tuntemus asiakkaan näkökulmasta. Olen erittäin iloinen siitä, että hän tulee mukaan Funidatan johtoryhmää", toteaa Funidatan toimitusjohtaja Mikko Myllys.

Hemminki-Reijonen johtaa nykyisin Helsingin yliopiston neljää opetusteknologian infrastruktuurin ja innovaatioiden tiimiä sekä yliopiston MOOC-keskusta. Hänen johtamansa asiantuntijatiimit vastaavat 11 tiedekunnan digitaalisista oppimisympäristöistä ja arviointiratkaisuista, tekoälypalveluista, opetusmediasta sekä Sisu-järjestelmän kehittämisestä ja tuesta. Nykyisen roolinsa kautta hänellä on vahva näkemys kotimaisen korkeakoulukentän digitaalisista palveluista ja niiden kehittämisestä.

title: How COST Short-Term Scientific Missions shape research journeys
content:
More than 2000+ Short-Term Scientific Missions (STSM) are funded yearly by COST. Open to researchers at all career stages, STSMs are one of COST’s most impactful networking tools. These scientific missions allow researchers involved in a COST Action to visit a university, a research institute or laboratory in another country to collaborate, access expertise and research infrastructure that may not be available at their home institution. 

Although these missions are called “short-term”, their impact often extends well beyond the exchange.  The Impact Assessment Study on Short-Term Mobility found that STSMs contribute to higher-quality research, developed skills, and new research collaborations, projects and proposals. Many STSMs also lead to joint publications between the visiting researcher and the host, or even common European or national research proposals. STSMs provide a good opportunity for both young and experienced researchers looking for mentoring and lifelong learning while helping institutions and COST Actions strengthen their networks, foster collaboration, and develop new scientific outputs.

title: Airy – Machine Intent in Motion
content:
Airy lässt zwei weiße Industrieroboter über einem schwebenden Seidentuch miteinander interagieren. Sie heben, spannen und lösen den Stoff, während sich ein Waldbild über seine Oberfläche bewegt. Die Bewegungen der Roboter verändern dabei die Atmosphäre des Raumes: Agieren sie im Einklang, lichtet sich der Himmel. Weichen ihre Bewegungen voneinander ab, ziehen Nebel und Sturm auf.

Die Installation untersucht, wie wir das Verhalten von Maschinen wahrnehmen und deuten. Durch Bewegung, Material und atmosphärische Veränderungen lädt Airy dazu ein, den Robotern eine eigene Handlungsfähigkeit zuzuschreiben – und darüber nachzudenken, wie Menschen und intelligente Maschinen miteinander in Beziehung treten und einander verstehen.

title: When Open Data Comes Full Circle: New OCR Reprocessing Software and Datasets Portal for Chronicling America
content:
Today’s guest post is from Nathan Yarasavage of the Serial and Government Publications Division at the Library of Congress.

True open-source collaboration is built on a simple principle: paying it forward. Last year, the Library of Congress announced a project to improve the quality of the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) text from some of the first newspapers digitized for Chronicling America. Now we are sharing our code. The NDNP-Open-OCR software is officially live on GitHub. This open-source release gives everyone access to a highly accurate, cost-effective, scalable OCR reprocessing solution that uses advanced layout detection to improve text quality.

To show what this new pipeline can do, we’ve already reprocessed over 425,000 pages and launched the brand-new Chronicling America Datasets portal. This new page provides direct access to our newly upgraded OCR text. It also serves as a gateway to downloadable bulk files for all 23+ million pages of historic news in the collection, opening new possibilities for computational research.

title: How the Beatles Made their Most Acclaimed Album, Revolver, Released 60 Years Ago This Month
content:
Among Beatles connoisseurs, it’s fair game to claim anything from Rubber Soul to Abbey Road as one’s favorite album. But even within that span of the catalog, a hierarchy of acclaim exists, and that hierarchy has been rearranged over the decades. The ecstatic reception of Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band lasted at least a decade. By the turn of the nineteen-eighties, its immediate predecessor Revolver had joined it at the top spot of critical regard; twenty years after that, Abbey Road had displaced Sgt. Pepper. Now, a full 60 years after it first came out, Revolver is the single Beatles album held in the highest esteem — which, naturally, makes it a serious contender for the greatest album ever recorded.

In his new video above, music YouTuber David Hartley explains what makes Revolver so beloved by recounting the history of its production. As in his previous Beatles videos, he draws on the library of studio outtakes that make audible the evolution of each song, as well as on contemporary interviews with the Beatles and their collaborators.

title: #KeepItOn @10: celebrating a decade of fighting internet shutdowns
content:
Internet shutdowns are widely viewed as an attack on human rights. But that wasn’t always the case. A decade ago, civil society groups  joined forces to push back against deliberate network disruptions, and today, the resistance to shutdowns is stronger than ever. As Access Now and the #KeepItOn community mark the 10th anniversary of the #KeepItOn campaign in 2026, we’re reflecting on the path travelled so far — and the journey still to come as we continue to fight to #KeepItOn around the world. 

Read on for a look at how the #KeepItOn campaign started, how it has evolved, and how you can join us to support and celebrate the work of the #KeepItOn coalition.

Ten years ago, there were no strong global norms condemning internet shutdowns. The groups fighting shutdowns were only loosely connected, and the lack of coordination made it difficult to get a global picture of the many harms people were experiencing — even as governments disconnected entire communities, disrupted business and daily life, undermined election integrity, exacerbated humanitarian crises, and attempted to hide grave human rights abuses and violations.

title: Mitä tekoälyn käyttöönottajan tulee tietää tekoälyasetuksen läpinäkyvyysvelvoitteista?
content:
Tekoälyn tuottaman ja muokkaaman sisällön läpinäkyvyys on noussut ajankohtaiseksi, kun EU:n tekoälyasetuksen (”AI Act”) 50 artiklan mukaiset läpinäkyvyysvelvoitteet tulivat sovellettaviksi 2.8.2026 alkaen. Tekoälyasetuksen velvoitteita on täsmennetty niin komission ohjeistuksella (Guidelines on transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems) kuin aikaisemmin kesäkuussa 2026 julkaistulla käytännesäännöstöllä (Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content).

Uutiset ja sosiaalinen media vilisevät erilaisia ohjeita ja vinkkejä – mitä tekoälyn läpinäkyvyyttä koskevista velvoitteista tulee tosiasiassa tietää? Tässä kirjoituksessa käymme läpi käyttöönottajan näkökulmasta, millainen sisältö tulee merkitä, miten merkitseminen toteutetaan ja miltä osin sääntely on velvoittavaa.

title: Who (or What) Generates Images for EFF?
content:
We’ve had a few questions from EFF supporters lately, asking whether the images we use on our blog posts, or on donation and shop items, have been created with AI image generators. We’d like to answer these questions and clarify our internal policy regarding image creation. 

EFF images are all made by human beings, not by automated image generators, with very rare exceptions. This is an internal decision made by our small design team, for the following reasons: 
  

  • Our designers bring knowledge and expertise to the images we create, informed by years of consultation with EFF’s lawyers, technologists and activists. We find that this informed perspective helps make the issues we cover more clear, and more engaging, for our supporters. 
  • The content on our sites is written by human beings, not by bots, and we feel that the images illustrating these posts should be human-made as well. Our supporters come to EFF for honest, trustworthy information from expert human beings, and we want our images to communicate that authenticity as well.

title: The backlash to social media bans has already begun
content:
Banning social media for minors has, well, gone viral. 

In less than a year, the world has witnessed a rapid-fire succession of political proposals to restrict youth access to social media: from the left-wing prime minister of Spain to the right-wing prime minister of Greece, the Australian Labor Party leader and a Texan Republican senator, and on to the national agendas of Brazil, Rwanda and, most recently, Vietnam.  

Creating new government limits to keep young people off digital platforms is increasingly seen as good politics, a popular piece of legislation that touts the protection of kids while tapping into bubbling anger at Big Tech platforms. Three decades into the digital era, policymakers around the world are converging on the idea that much of the time we spend online is not good for us — and that children are the most vulnerable. 

Yet eight months since Australia’s groundbreaking under-16 social media ban triggered a surge of similar legislation around the world, doubts are already spreading about both the efficacy and unintended side effects of a blanket ban.
snippet: Banning social media for minors has, well, gone viral.

title: Lebanon Issues New Charges Against Former Central Bank Chief Riad Salame
content:
A Lebanese judge has issued new charges against former central bank governor Riad Salame and a former commercial banker over allegations of financial crimes, including embezzlement, money laundering, bribery, and illicit enrichment, according to Lebanon’s National News Agency.

On Monday, Judge Raja Hamouche filed proceedings against 76-year-old Salame and Samir Hanna, 88, the former head of Bank Audi, one of Lebanon's largest banks. The allegations include the creation of shell companies, misappropriating funds belonging to the Central Bank, and the fraudulent use of those funds to purchase shares and bonds in commercial banks. He also charged them with illicit enrichment, money laundering, and bribery.

The Public Prosecutor of Appeal requested an arrest warrant against Salame. Media have reported that he is currently under medical supervision at a hospital in Beirut. He has repeatedly denied all charges against him. His lawyer has not responded to OCCRP’s request for comment.

Hanna, 88, has reportedly already paid a $1 million bail and is not in custody. He could not be reached for comment.

title: Is There Anyone Who Can Respond to My FOIA Requests? Anyone?
content:
I file a lot of Freedom of Information Act requests. I’ve been requesting staff lists from both Trump administrations, and I have tracked thousands of federal political appointees in order to publish financial disclosures in searchable databases. 

Much of that data was sourced from the Office of Personnel Management, which maintains a trove of information about who works in the federal government. But that agency’s FOIA department was thrown into chaos as Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency fanned out across federal agencies to cut employees in early 2025.

Getting records from the agency has since become an increasingly Kafkaesque process, one that in early July of this year bounced me between three different seemingly abandoned email inboxes and two web portals. Aside from the fact that my once-routine requests now languish for months, just asking for documents has become its own kind of shell game.

“They just let the whole Privacy team go,” a now-former FOIA specialist at OPM told me by email in February 2025, referring to public records office staff. The specialist was cut the next day.

title: Danitello: Maailmanluokan ponnistus
content:
Eletään 2000-luvun puoliväliä. Ala-asteikäinen Daniel Okas painaa sisarustensa kanssa hirveää kyytiä polkupyörällä kouluun.

Lunta on tullut edellisenä yönä rutkasti, ja pyöräily on tuskastuttavan hidasta. Hiki kastelee pienen pojan paidanselkää sekä fyysisen suorituksen että henkisen paineen takia.

En kai minä myöhästy?

Okas polkee ja sättii itseään itku kurkussa. Olisi pitänyt lähteä aiemmin!

Hän pääsee koulun pihalle, jättää pyörän ja porhaltaa luokkaan, mutta kellon on armoton: Okas on kolme minuuttia myöhässä.

Se hävettää ihan tolkuttomasti, tuntuu maailmanlopulta. Koska hän ei ole se poika, joka on myöhässä! Hän on ajoissa, kunnollinen, hän hoitaa hommat.

Okas on ala-asteikäisenä ottanut ensimmäisen oppitunnin kurssilla, jonka tavoitteena on breikata kansainvälisesti musiikkialalla.

Oppitunti numero yksi: älä myöhästy.

Kelataan parikymmentä vuotta eteenpäin. Daniel ”Danitello” Okas (s. 1998) istuu studiollaan Herttoniemessä Fountain Productionsin tiloissa.

Pari päivää sitten juhlittiin. Kesän alussa Danitellon tuottamassa ja kirjoittamassa musiikissa paukkui nimittäin 1 000 000 000 streamauksen raja.

”Se on ihan hullua”, Okas sanoo.

title: Hae mukaan SAFAn mentorointiohjelmaan 2026-2027
content:
SAFAn suositun mentorointiohjelman seuraava kierros käynnistyy syksyllä. Haemme mukaan aktoreita sekä mentoreita.

Ohjelma koostuu SAFAn järjestämistä etätapahtumista sekä kahdenkeskisistä tapaamisista. Mentori-aktori -parit sopivat itseään kiinnostavat aihealueet ja keskustelevat niistä haluamassaan laajuudessa oman aikataulunsa mukaan. Keskusteluissa tietoa ja osaamista – etenkin niin sanottua hiljaista tietoa – siirretään kokeneemmalta kokemattomammalle.

Aktorin eli mentoroitavan täytyy olla vähintään maisterivaiheen opiskelija. title: YK:n seuraava pääsihteeri on monella tapaa poikkeuksellinen: ehkä nainen, pitkästä aikaa globaalista etelästä – ja ennennäkemättömän haasteen edessä
content:
YK:n uuden pääsihteerin on sanottu perivän aina jonkin kriisin. Seuraavalla, tammikuussa virkaansa astuvalla pääsihteerillä, on edessään kuitenkin aivan erityisen suuren kriisin ratkaiseminen.

”Seuraava pääsihteeri perii jotain syvempää kuin sarjan kriisejä. Hän perii luottamuskriisin, joka kohdistuu monenkeskiseen järjestelmään sinänsä”, tiivistää Farah Munayer, globaalin etelän ajatushautomoja edustavan Southern Voice -verkoston strategiakoordinaattori. 

Maailmalla riittää nyt kriisejä: YK:lla on akuutti rahoituspula. Turvallisuusneuvosto ei saa eripuraisuutensa takia päätöksiä tehtyä, ja koko kansainväliseen sopimiseen perustuvaa järjestelmää haastetaan Venäjän ja Yhdysvaltain johdolla. Samalla pitäisi ratkaista ilmastonmuutos, luontokato, eriarvoisuus ja konfliktit. 

”Ainakin tehokkuuden parantaminen tulee olemaan pääsihteerin agendalla – ja samalla luottamuksen palauttaminen maailmanjärjestöön ja toivottavasti myös suurvaltojen välille. Koko YK:n toimintaa leimaa kuitenkin polarisaatio ja se, että se ei pysty tuottamaan niitä palveluita, joita se on luvannut”, arvioi myös Ulkopoliittisen instituutin ohjelmajohtaja, tutkija Katja Creutz.

title: How polarised is European politics? Here’s how your generation, gender and where you live affect what you believe
content:
Across Europe, the political debate has rarely looked more polarised. Media narratives frequently describe societies as becoming sharply divided between younger progressive and older conservative generations.

A growing body of research also suggests that political attitudes are becoming more divided by gender, particularly among younger cohorts. Young women seem to be adopting more liberal positions than young men on issues such as climate change and immigration.

Using data from the European Social Survey, which I have led since 2013, my team has examined the truth of these claims. We’ve done this by looking at long-term trends across eastern, western and northern Europe between 2002 and 2023 in relation to political orientation, climate change fears and attitudes towards immigration.

Political orientation over time by age and gender

Across all country groups, younger respondents consistently place themselves further to the left on the political orientation scale than older respondents.
