title: Would Ted Lasso be a good sports coach in real life?
content:
Ted Lasso is back: the hugely successful Apple TV series has returned for a fourth season.

The sports comedy-drama – which follows an American football coach with zero soccer experience who is hired to run a struggling English Premier League team – has become a cultural phenomenon. It has won 13 Emmy Awards and was the most-watched original streaming show in the United States in 2023.

In Season 4, Ted faces a new challenge: coaching a second-division women’s soccer team.

The show’s popularity raises an interesting question for anyone involved in sport: would Ted Lasso actually be a good coach in real life?

Outwardly, Ted hardly fits the traditional image of a hard-nosed elite sports coach. He is relentlessly optimistic, talks about feelings and seems more interested in people than tactics.

For decades, successful coaching was often associated with authority, toughness and control.

But successful modern coaches such as Steve Kerr in the US National Basketball Association (NBA) and Chris Fagan in the Australian Football League (AFL) have challenged this model, speaking openly about vulnerability, empathy and genuine relationships with their players.
snippet: Ted Lasso is back: the hugely successful Apple TV series has returned for a fourth season.
creator: Vincent Kelly, Associate Professor, Queensland University of Technology

title: The Tantalizing Possibility Of Locating Consciousness In The Brain
content:
It is past midnight in a fluorescent-lit office. A neuroscientist opens ChatGPT and uploads the seventh version of a paper, which is littered with critical notes from a peer reviewer. “Why is Reviewer #2 such an idiot?” the neuroscientist asks the chatbot. The reply comes instantly, witty and sympathetic, reframing the criticism in a way that puts everything into perspective. The neuroscientist laughs, then pauses.

How can this computer seem so very human? It demonstrates abilities we usually associate with intelligent beings: language, abstraction, social inference, even a sense of humor. The design of modern chatbots was inspired by the neocortex, the pinnacle of mammalian evolution, so their human-like behavior should not have come as a complete surprise. But what few anticipated was that such complex behavior could emerge in the complete absence of biological neurons.

title: Enemmän elämää
content:
Maailma on monimutkainen paikka. Epävarmuudet ja -selvyydet uhkaavat välillä halvaannuttaa.

Siksi ajoittain on hyvä muistaa yksinkertaisia nyrkkisääntöjä. Yksi niistä on tavoitella kokonaisuutena enemmän elämää.

Ekologisen kestävyyskriisin taustalla on pohjimmiltaan elämän näivettäminen. Ihminen on pitkään nakertanut metsiä, ryöstökalastanut meriä, ojittanut soita ja padonnut jokia.

Suunta pitää kääntää niin luonnon kuin ihmisen itsensäkin takia. Siinä auttaa, jos asettaa tavoitteeksi edistää enemmän elämää.

Enemmän elämää voi tarkoittaa sekä määrää että laatua. Määrän voi karkeasti pelkistää biomassaan, elollisen aineksen määrään. Laatua voi mitata elämän monimuotoisuudella, kuten lajien kirjolla.

Enemmän elämää on aina suhteessa johonkin. Asfaltin voi vaihtaa avoimeen soramaahan, soran nurmikkoon. Nurmikon voi leikata harvemmin tai korvata niityllä. Niityn sijaan voi istuttaa kerroksellisen mikrometsän – ja niin edelleen.

Vastaavasti käytännössä yksilajisessa talousmetsässä rinnalle voi ottaa toisen puulajin. Kahdesta lajista voi pyrkiä kohti kolmea tai viittä – tai kymmentä.

title: Strategies To Seek Funding For Investigative Journalism
content:
We are in a challenging environment for investigative journalism. The need for investigative reporting exceeds reliable funding sources for it in many parts of the world. Nonetheless, investigative journalists are approaching the challenges with creativity and resilience, and have multiple paths to explore to seek funding. This session will provide a kind of decision tree or logic to help journalists determine what paths may be worth exploring to find story and project funding in their region or topic. Our talk is aimed at individual journalists who have not done fundraising for their work and are seeking advice on where to get started. We’ll explore key considerations and pathways you can choose depending on your circumstances to explore funding options and pursue those that may fit for you and support the journalism you seek to produce.

This session will not provide suggestions or lists of specific funding sources.  Funding options vary greatly by country, region and even your own individual situations. However, a tip sheet will provide links to global organizations that can help you research grant options, examples of journalism networks and networked funders and some other tips.

title: Fiscal Multipliers and the Effects of Consolidation Measures in Finland
content: Finland faces chronic fiscal deficits, rising public debt, and weak economic growth, making fiscal consolidation an urgent priority. This report reviews the international research literature on fiscal multipliers and consolidation programs and estimates fiscal multipliers for categories of public expenditure and taxation in Finland using time-series methods, drawing on a new quarterly dataset for 1999–2025 compiled by Statistics Finland. Based on the key empirical findings of this study, the expenditure multiplier of fiscal policy in Finland is relatively large, and the tax multiplier is remarkably large, which is likely reinforced by the institutional environment of the country, namely, the high tax-to-GDP ratio and its euro area membership. Among expenditure categories, public investment carries the largest multiplier, making cuts to it especially costly for the economy. Increases in consumption and corporate income taxes also seem to generate large output losses. The results highlight a central tension in economic policy: stabilising public finances requires fiscal consolidation, but consolidation weakens economic growth in the short run. Therefore, the effects of fiscal consolidation depend crucially on its composition, timing, and supporting policy measures. Fiscal consolidation should not be seen merely as a combination of expenditure cuts and tax increases, but as a broader economic policy program in which consolidation is combined with reforms that strengthen economic growth, employment, competitiveness, and the long-term sustainability of public finances.

Pressmeddelande på svenska

Metson ja teeren koko maan tiheydet ovat lähellä edellisvuoden tasoa ja pitkäaikaisia keskiarvojaan. title: 226 Ansel Adams Photographs of Great American National Parks Are Now Online
content:
Like many American stories, the story of the National Parks begins with pillage, death, deep cultural misunderstanding, and venture capitalism. According to Ken Burns’ film series The National Parks: America’s Best Idea, we can date the idea back to 1851, with the “discovery” of Yosemite by a marauding armed battalion that entered the land “searching for Indians, intent on driving the natives from their homelands and onto reservations.” The Mariposa Battalion, led by Captain James D. Savage, set fire to the Indians’ homes and storehouses after they had retreated to the mountains, “in order to starve them into submission.”

One member of the battalion, a doctor named Lafayette Bunnell, found himself entranced by the scenery amidst this destruction. “As I looked, a peculiar exalted sensation seemed to fill my whole being,” he wrote in his later accounts, “and I found myself in tears with emotion.” He named the place “Yosemite,” thinking it was the name of the Indian tribe the soldiers sought to force out or eradicate. The word, it turned out “meant something entirely different,” referring to people who should be feared: “It means, ‘they are killers.’”

title: Türkiye Seeks to Transfer US Cluster Munitions to Ukraine
content:
(Washington, DC, August 11, 2026) – Türkiye has requested permission from the United States to “retransfer” to Ukraine tens of thousands of cluster munition rockets, missiles, and artillery projectiles that have been in Türkiye’s stockpiles for decades, Human Rights Watch said today. 

These weapons, which contain over 10 million explosive submunitions, were originally produced in part by Türkiye under licenses from the US initiated in 1987. The artillery projectiles that make up the bulk of the proposed deal were removed from US service in 1994, when the howitzers that fired this ammunition were retired from US service.

“Dumping obsolete cluster munitions into a conflict creates a humanitarian liability for civilians that is tragically foreseeable,” said Nicole Widdersheim, deputy Washington director at Human Rights Watch. “The impact on civilians of these more than 30-year-old inaccurate and unreliable munitions is what motivated 112 countries to ban the weapon by joining the international Convention on Cluster Munitions.”

title: French Prosecution Says Alleged 'DZ Mafia' Gang Leader Arrested in Algeria
content:
Algerian authorities have arrested an alleged leader of the ‘DZ Mafia,’ an organized crime syndicate linked to a wave of drug violence in France. Mehdi Laribi, a French-Algerian national, was arrested in Algeria in late July under an arrest warrant issued by investigating magistrates from the Marseille Public Prosecutor's Office. 

The Marseille Public Prosecutor's Office confirmed to OCCRP that Laribi “was detained by Algerian authorities on July 20” and placed under judicial supervision by the Algerian justice system the following day. 

“This action was taken pursuant to an arrest warrant issued by investigating magistrates in connection with the "Octopus” operation handled by the Marseille courts—which concerns the structure of the ‘DZ Mafia’.”

French prosecutors accuse the DZ Mafia of operating a widespread criminal network involved in drug trafficking, kidnapping, and contract killings. Named after Algeria's alpha-2 country code (DZ) in reference to its founders' origins, the group originated in Marseille's housing projects before expanding into several other French cities.

title: Elvish, Klingon and Pig Latin: what can invented languages teach us about the human brain?
content:
Invented languages tend to be the stuff of fantasy or science fiction worlds. But as a child, you may have made one up yourself.

Take Pig Latin, which involves moving the starting consonant of a word to the end and adding an “-ay” sound. “Pig Latin” thus becomes “ig-pay atin-lay”, while words beginning with a vowel have a “-way” at the end. With a little practice, you can hold entire conversations in Pig Latin.

However, creating new forms of communication goes far beyond children’s games or brain exercises. Throughout history, people have invented or adapted languages – whether out of necessity, creativity, or scientific interest.

The process of creating a language can also offer a window onto how our brains work. From the code-speak of children’s games to “miniature” languages designed in laboratories, all new forms of communication reveal something about our ability to learn and adopt new rules.

Many novel languages are not born in offices or laboratories, but at points where multiple cultures meet. When two communities with different languages need to communicate in order to trade or simply coexist, a simplified version of language emerges known as a pidgin.

title: On the Open Science Framework's changes - Chris Hartgerink, PhD
content:
"The OSF was pivotal to the early days of reforming research around 2012-2017. I used it a lot for a while, and ultimately used it through its integrations only. It added some great services and some not so great ones. I did not always agree with their approach, but I was often glad they existed.

The OSF has had many failings over the years and I think it is great they're making a decision on the role it has in 2026 and beyond. To me, the decision to unwind projects is a reflection of the fact that they did not really connect with the userbase to understand the needs of researchers, while riding on the tide that they served the researcher's needs. They gobbled up tens of millions of dollars for their operations. The fact that this announcement came as a surprise, is a highlight of how disconnected the development was from the people they claim to serve."

title: GIJN Masterclass Round-Up: Data Journalism
content:
GIJN’s Global Academy is your gateway to investigative journalism training. Through masterclass videos, training programs (in person or online), webinars or mentorship programs, the Academy helps journalists at every stage strengthen their investigative skills, connect with peers, and continue learning. In this post, we’ve gathered some of our recent expert masterclass videos that tackle different aspects of using data in your investigations.

In this masterclass video, Fabiola Torres, founder and director of Salud con Lupa, shares a practical approach to data journalism, starting not with tools, but with documents.

She explains how investigations often begin with access to information requests, and how journalists must build their own datasets from messy, fragmented sources like PDFs. Using simple tools like spreadsheets and keyword searches, she shows how to organize, analyze, and extract insights from large volumes of information.

This grounded, hands-on guide cuts through the hype to help: master the basics, trust your reporting instincts, and turn raw data into impactful investigations.

title: Vietnam: Reject Repressive Penal Code Revisions
content:
(Bangkok) – Vietnamese authorities should reject proposed revisions to the penal code that violate basic rights, Human Rights Watch said today. The authorities should instead amend the law to comply with international human rights standards.

Vietnam’s Ministry of Public Security submitted the draft code to the National Assembly for review during the session from August 3 to 24, 2026, with the expectation that the revised code would be adopted after October 20. The draft revisions would increase already harsh penalties for vague and overbroad criminal offenses that infringe upon the right to freedom of expression and other rights.

“The Vietnamese National Assembly should reject the Ministry of Public Security’s draft revised criminal code and all rights-violating articles that the authorities frequently use to silence critics,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Freedom of expression means that people are able to voice opinions critical of the government without fear of punishment.”

title: Albania's Cheerful 'AI Minister' Is the Product of a Government Agency Under Investigation for Massive Corruption
content:
Last September, Albania made headlines around the world when it introduced the world’s first-ever “AI minister.”

Diella, which means “Sun” in Albanian, was a chatbot that had been promoted to ministerial status. Her remit, Prime Minister Edi Rama announced, was to ensure that “public tenders will be 100 percent free of corruption.”

“I do not have personal ambitions or interests,” the AI avatar, who dresses in traditional costume, told parliament in her maiden speech. “I only have data, a thirst for knowledge, and algorithms dedicated to serving citizens… free from prejudice, discrimination, clientelism, nepotism, or corruption.” 

At the time, there were doubts over whether Diella could offer any real solution to Albania’s long-standing corruption problem. 

It appears that some of the reservations may have been well-founded. Experts caution that Albania’s plan to use Diella as a buffer against corruption has flaws, given that information generated by AI is not inherently neutral, and that there has been little transparency so far on how the technology will be deployed.

title: Väitös: Etäkuntoutuksen onnistumista ei ratkaista pelkällä teknologialla
content:
Koronapandemia vauhditti etäkuntoutuksen käyttöönottoa Suomessa. Samalla paljastui, että teknologia yksin ei ratkaise etäkuntoutuksen onnistumista. TtM Tuija Partanen osoittaa väitöstutkimuksessaan, että etäkuntoutuksen onnistuminen riippuu teknologian, tehtävien, asiakkaiden, ammattilaisten ja toimintaympäristön yhteensopivuudesta. Tuloksissa korostuvat toimintaympäristön merkitys, läheisten kaksoisrooli sekä ammattilaisten monitehtävä- ja moniosaamisen vaatimukset.

Etäkuntoutus on osa sosiaali- ja terveydenhuollon digitaalista murrosta, joka muuttaa kuntoutuspalveluiden toimintaympäristöä, käytäntöjä sekä asiakkaiden ja ammattilaisten osaamisvaatimuksia. Tuija Partasen väitöstutkimuksessa tarkastellaan, miten etäkuntoutus otettiin käyttöön Suomessa COVID-19-pandemian alkuvaiheessa ja millaiset sosiotekniset tekijät vaikuttivat sen onnistumiseen.

Partasen tutkimuksessa tarkastellaan etäkuntoutuksen käyttöönottoa yksilöterapiaa toteuttavien ammattilaisten kokemana. Tutkimusaineisto kerättiin kyselytutkimuksella keväällä 2020 fysioterapeuteilta, toimintaterapeuteilta, puheterapeuteilta, musiikkiterapeuteilta, neuropsykologeilta ja psykoterapeuteilta.

title: OSF is Changing: What's changing, what's continuing, and where to find guidance
content: "We are preparing substantial changes to OSF that will reduce its functionality, focus OSF on its unique strengths, and move toward an integrated model with complementary services like Zenodo, a repository for researchers to share data, materials, and code hosted by CERN, for researchers to do open science. As part of that shift, the OSF Projects workflow – the part of the OSF used for project collaboration, file management, and storage – is being phased out as an active workspace. This change does not affect persistence and accessibility of existing public projects. We are very sorry for the disruption that this will cause for OSF users. These changes are necessary because of a challenging funding environment for open research infrastructure. Important background about why we are making this change is available in a separate post. Our priorities are to support the long-term discovery and access of content publicly shared on OSF so it remains persistent, discoverable, and accessible, and to ease the transition for users to continue doing open science. title: Librarians as Creators of Open Educational Resources for Advanced Searching
content: Abstract:  Health librarians are increasingly authoring their own open educational resources (OERs) to teach advanced literature searching—an essential skill for evidence synthesis. These instructional materials, often created in response to gaps in existing resources, go beyond simple guides incorporating bilingual content, scaffolded exercises, knowledge checks, and video tutorials. They reflect librarians’ deep expertise and commitment to affordable, open, and high-quality learning materials. This panel will explore three librarian-led OER projects that exemplify this growing trend. Through brief presentations and a moderated discussion, panelists will share insights into the design, implementation, and impact of their work, and reflect on the broader implications of OER creation as a scholarly and pedagogical practice.

title: Various European Commission consultations
content:
An Open Web Data Infrastructure for Europe: We’re actively helping to shape European policy and legislation!

We completed the OpenWebSearch.EU project in April this year. Nevertheless, the OpenWebSearch Initiative, which brings together many partners from the OWS project and new stakeholders from research and industry, continues to work tirelessly on and for the Open Web Index (OWI).

The initiative not only aims to develop the infrastructure further, but is also committed to creating the framework conditions for a European Web Data Infrastructure. Shaping European policy and influencing legislation in support of an open European Web Data Infrastructure are, and will remain, key tasks of the initiative and the OSF.

We take every opportunity to emphasize the importance of a web data infrastructure for Europe!

With this mission in mind, we have, over the past few months, submitted comments on various European Commission consultations in collaboration with the OpenWebSearch Initiative and the PriDI project. In these consultations, citizens and other stakeholders can provide feedback on the Commission’s planned policy and legislative initiatives.

title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 review: your passport to a folding phone future
content:
Novel squat Android opens to an iPad-like screen for video or multitasking, with plenty of power and battery life

Samsung’s latest folding phone breaks the mould with a squat, passport-like shape reminiscent of the Blackberry, which opens up to become a tablet similar to an iPad mini. It is certainly a better shape for a tablet than other designs, but is a short and wide phone when closed a compromise too far?

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is an entirely new variant in Samsung’s foldable family for this year launched alongside the Z Fold 8 Ultra with a more familiar candy bar shape. Both folders are extremely expensive, with the Fold 8 starting at £1,699 (€1,999/$1,899.99/A$2,699) and the Fold 8 Ultra at £1,899 (€2,199/$2,099.99/A$2,999), with RAMageddon driving up prices even at the top of the market.

title: ASF-tutkimustulokset varmistuneet EU:n vertailulaboratoriossa
content:
EU:n afrikkalaisen sikaruton vertailulaboratorio (Centro de Investigación en Sanidad Animal, CISA-INIA/CSIC, Espanja) on vahvistanut Ruokavirastossa todetut maan ensimmäiset afrikkalaisen sikaruton tautitapaukset.

Ruokaviraston eläintautivirologian laboratorio on sekvensoinut Virolahdelta kuolleena löydettyjen villisikojen näytteissä todetun afrikkalaisen sikaruttoviruksen koko genomin. Sekvenssianalyysit osoittavat, että virus kuuluu genotyyppiin II ja tarkemmin sen geneettiseen ryhmään 3. Analyysi perustuu genomin kuuteen muuntelevaan alueeseen (CVR, IGR, O174L, K145R, MGF ja ECO2).

Geneettistä ryhmää 3 on raportoitu ensimmäisen kerran Ukrainassa 2012. Vuodesta 2014 lähtien sitä on esiintynyt Baltian maissa vuosittain, ja tapauksia on todettu myös mm. Puolassa, Tšekissä, Romaniassa, Unkarissa, Belgiassa, Italiassa ja Venäjällä. Viruksen geneettisen analyysin perusteella ei voida vahvistaa viruksen maahantuloreittiä.

title: The Source: Where Curiosity Sparks Discovery
content:
The drawers from the card catalog are meant to surprise you.

Open one, and a tornado from “The Wizard of Oz” swirls to life. Another reveals a rocket launch. A third shows Rosa Parks’ pancake recipe.

At The Source, the Library’s first-of-its-kind experiential research gallery for young people, the familiar wooden card catalog becomes an entry point into history, inviting visitors to explore the past not as something dusted off in a dog-eared textbook but as something they can actively discover.

Here, the past unfolds in multiple formats. Voices echo from across time, and collection items pull young visitors into the role of budding researchers. From the moment they enter the ground floor of the Jefferson Building, they can ask questions, make connections and explore history through a blend of nostalgia and modern technology.

title: How the Bird Sound Effects in Alfred Hitchcock’s The Birds Were Created with a Pioneering Electronic Instrument, the Trautonium
content:
Alfred Hitchcock’s The Birds was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Special Effects, though viewers raised on more recent Hollywood spectacles would hardly find its mechanized and optically printed avian attackers convincing. Still, the picture as a whole has retained its eerie, ominous power over the last six decades, and a decent amount of the credit for that goes to an aspect that hasn’t dated at all: its non-musical “score” by the early electronic composer Oskar Sala. Many of the threatening bird calls on the soundtrack were actually played by Sala on a device called the Mixtur-Trautonium, a pre-synthesizer orchestral electronic instrument of which he wasn’t just the undisputed master, but the only player in existence.

After his acceptance into the Berlin Conservatory in 1929, Sala came into contact with the Trautonium, which had recently been invented by one Dr. Friedrich Trautwein. Inspired to more deeply understand the principles behind the nascent technology of electronic music, and to further it, he went on to study physics at the University of Berlin in the mid-nineteen-thirties.

title: 25 Years of Partnership: CC at Wikimania 2026
content:
With both Wikipedia and Creative Commons turning 25 this year, our participation in Wikimania 2026 felt especially meaningful. A quarter-century in, both organizations have evolved from scrappy experiments to global infrastructure. Our community has grown through a shared commitment to openness, access, and knowledge. The weeklong conference reaffirmed that commitment as AI is reshaping how we access knowledge and share online.

During the conference, CC hosted both a pre-conference salon celebrating our 25th Anniversary and a workshop during the main conference discussing collective action in the age of AI. CC staff also spoke on multiple panels throughout the week that addressed the effects of AI crawling on human creativity and sharing, the coordination gap between cultural institutions and generative AI, and training on CC’s global advocacy for the Open Heritage Statement.

title: Call for Contributions: Newsfluencers and Public Interest Media
content:
The Forum on Information and Democracy (FID) is preparing an insight report examining the relationship between news content creators (or so called “newsfluencers”) and public interest journalism and welcomes contributions from experts.

The report will look at how the creator economy is reshaping the information ecosystem: the competitive and financial pressures it places on traditional media, the spectrum of actors – from independent journalists to entertainment-driven influencers, the strategies newsrooms are adopting to compete or collaborate with creators, and the policy frameworks that could help news content creators become allies of information integrity.

We welcome contributions from researchers, journalists, media organizations, platforms, policymakers, and content creators themselves, including:

  • Reports, studies, or data on the creator economy’s impact on news media business models and audience behavior
  • Analysis or case studies on news content creators’ editorial practices, self-regulation, or professional norms
  • Examples of media-creator partnerships, transformation strategies, or creator studios

title: Real Estate Transactions Breakfast 9.9.2026
content:
After years of subdued activity in the wake of the zero-interest rate era, the transactional real estate market in Finland is showing signs of recovery. According to KTI, the total transaction volume of the first half of 2026 amounted to some €3.5 billion, which is significantly higher than in the two previous years. Residential properties were the most traded property sector in January-June 2026, accounting for some 45% of the total volume, followed by industrial and retail properties. Foreign investment has remained strong overall, with especially Swedish investors returning to the market after the relatively attractive yields offered by Finnish assets. Are these signs of better times to come?

title: Meta Must Stop Silencing Reproductive Health Information
content:
Access to accurate information about reproductive and maternal health can be critical. But on Meta's platforms, simply talking about prescription medication, abortion care, or one's own medical experiences can be enough to trigger content removals and account restrictions.

That's why EFF recently submitted a public comment to the Meta Oversight Board in its consideration of a case involving an Instagram post about prescription drugs during pregnancy and childbirth. The case touches upon a topic we’ve been documenting for some time; last year we collected stories from individuals who had experienced censorship of reproductive health information on various platforms. Meta in particular stood out: Its moderation systems routinely fail to distinguish between prohibited drug transactions and legitimate discussion of medications, including educational information and people's firsthand experiences with healthcare.

title: EU opens channel with Meta, TikTok to tackle Ceuta migrant crisis
content:
The EU, Meta and TikTok on Monday agreed to create a dedicated channel with fact-checkers to flag disinformation linked to a surge of migrants arriving in Spanish territory, three people told POLITICO.

Thousands of migrants arrived in late July in Ceuta, a Spanish enclave in Morocco and the EU’s only land border with Africa. The influx was triggered by false narratives spreading online that told migrants they would be welcomed, according to fact-checking site Maldita.es.

The Commission met with representatives from TikTok and Meta on Friday and Monday to coordinate a response to disinformation online. They agreed to set up an “enhanced information exchange and cooperation mechanism for reducing the impact of disinformation on the Ceuta crisis,” said the three people with direct knowledge of the talks, who were granted anonymity to speak freely.

title: US Activates Long Unused Deportation Court
content:
The United States government has filed its first application ever with the Alien Terrorist Removal Court (ATRC). The court’s chief judge today canceled a scheduled hearing to decide whether Nazira Haji Zada, a 47-year-old green card holder from Afghanistan who has been held without charge since July 28, should remain in federal custody while proceedings continue.

The ATRC is a specialized federal court created in 1996 to hear deportation proceedings against noncitizens suspected of terrorism in which the government wants to use undisclosed classified evidence. Court rules do not allow challenges to the evidence even if unlawfully obtained. Government lawyers allege that Zada pledged loyalty to the Islamic State (also known as ISIS) but have not charged her with any crime. She ultimately could be deported on the basis of a preponderance of evidence that she was an “alien terrorist.” Her lawyers have stated that only a summary of the evidence against her has been made available to them. US courts have repeatedly found that using secret evidence in deportation proceedings violates due process.

title: The Battle for Believability
content:
Why Trust Has Become the World’s Most Valuable Strategic Resource

By Ramesh Jaura

This article was first published on https://rjaura.substack.com/

BERLIN | 10 August 2026 (IDN) — The most serious problem of the AI age might not lie in the ease with which lies can be produced, but in the increasing difficulty of believing in the truth. When a voter hears a familiar voice in a piece of footage, they pause for thought. A parent seeing a disturbing picture on their phone begins to question whether or not to pass it on. A journalist who receives a recording must now begin by wondering if it is genuine.

Ordinary people scrolling through social media are confronted with viral videos that may be digitally altered or entirely fabricated. Friends send each other photos in group chats that look real but could easily have been made by an app. Even a neighbour’s message in a local WhatsApp group can spark debate over whether the evidence it contains can be trusted.

The traditional ‘credibility gap’ revealed a loss of trust in government; today’s crisis is more severe since it is the same kind of system intended to determine what is real that is now itself being doubted.

title: How data journalism is done on TikTok: six key takeaways from watching 50 videos
content:
Short-form vertical video is quickly becoming a key format for telling all types of news stories — and data journalism is no exception.

As a data journalist, I wanted to know how these outlets use this new and evolving digital video format to create “data shorts”: short-form social media videos in a vertical, reel-style format, that analyses or reports on specific datasets or newly released data.

I analysed 50 data shorts from the TikTok accounts of five major UK news publications — the BBC, ITV News, Guardian, Times and Financial Times — to examine how these digital news outlets approach the format. I looked at the genre of story they covered, the angles they focused on, their length, and their use of animation, to help inform my guidelines.

My analysed data shorts averaged a runtime of just under 84 seconds.

The BBC ranked lowest for average video length, at just under a minute, while the Financial Times had the highest at 105 seconds.

Notably, none of the publications had an average video length over two minutes, despite TikTok allowing longer uploads up to 60 minutes.
snippet: Short-form vertical video is quickly becoming a key format for telling all types of news stories — and data journalism is no exception.

title: Alleged Irish Crime Boss Charged After UAE Extradition
content:
Alleged Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan was extradited from the United Arab Emirates to Ireland on Sunday and charged with directing the activities of a criminal organization.

Kinahan, 49, appeared before Dublin’s non-jury Special Criminal Court less than two hours after arriving aboard an Irish government jet, according to coverage by Irish Times security and crime editor Conor Lally. Kinahan was remanded in custody at the maximum-security Portlaoise Prison and is due to appear in court again on October 5.

He faces a single charge of directing a criminal organization between October 18, 2015, and April 6, 2017. Kinahan has not entered a plea, but has previously denied being a crime boss.

The Irish Times reported that Kinahan did not have a lawyer at the hearing. When Judge Patrick McGrath asked about the lack of legal representation, Kinahan said: “I didn’t have time to arrange anything.” He explained that he had been isolated in a Dubai prison before the extradition and had expected a relative to contact a lawyer.

After the judge explained that any application for bail would have to be made to the High Court, Kinahan replied: “I think we know I won’t be getting bail.”

title: More Than Half the Homes in East Omaha Have Unsafe Lead Levels. That Doesn’t Mean the EPA Will Clean Them Up.
content:
Despite hundreds of millions of dollars spent on environmental cleanup, more than half the yards in a section of Omaha, Nebraska, that used to surround a lead smelter still have enough contamination to cause high blood-lead levels in kids, according to tests by the Flatwater Free Press and ProPublica.

The findings were consistent across the city’s older urban core — in the historically Black neighborhoods north of downtown, the predominantly Hispanic areas to the south and the more white and affluent areas in midtown. However, homes closest to where a lead smelter and other downtown factories operated tended to have slightly higher concentrations than those farther out.

As part of the Environmental Protection Agency’s Superfund program, the federal government and the city of Omaha have been attempting to remove lead from Omaha’s yards since the late 1990s.

title: Ilmoittaudu luvanhakua helpottavalle tekijälistalle OmaSanastossa
content:
Sanaston tavoitteena on tehdä kirjallisuuden käyttölupien hankkimisesta mahdollisimman sujuvaa. Sanasto voi kuitenkin myöntää lupia vain edustamiensa tekijöiden tekstien käyttöön. Aiemmin luvanhakijat saivat vasta hakemuksen jätettyään tietää, voiko kaikkiin teksteihin saada luvat Sanaston kautta. Esimerkiksi kirjastojen tapahtumissa luetaan monesti useiden tekijöiden teoksia. Tällöin hakemusten täyttäminen voi viedä paljon aikaa. 

Helpottaakseen luvanhakijoiden työtä Sanasto on vuodesta 2024 lähtien julkaissut verkossa suostumuksensa antaneiden edustamiensa tekijöiden nimet. Listan avulla luvanhakija voi jo käyttöä suunnitellessaan tarkistaa, voiko Sanasto myöntää luvan suunniteltuihin teksteihin. Verkossa on tällä hetkellä yli 1 200 tekijän nimet. 

Lista on avoimesti saatavilla verkossa. Siinä julkaistaan vain niiden tekijöiden nimet, jotka ovat antaneet siihen suostumuksensa erillisellä kyselylomakkeella. Muita tietoja, kuten yhteystietoja, ei julkaista. Tekijän nimen yhteydessä näkyy kuitenkin muutama hänen teoksensa. Mahdollisuudesta liittyä listalle on kerrottu asiakkaiden uutiskirjeissä, ja käytetyimpien teosten tekijöille on lähetetty lisäksi henkilökohtainen sähköposti.

content:

Koska suomalaiset ovat yhä enemmistönä, he myös jossain määrin dominoivat residenssin toimintaa.

title: Women can lead with both heart and mind. Here’s why compassionate leadership matters now
content: When former New Zealand prime minister and activist Jacinda Ardern rejected the idea that empathy makes a leader weak, she named a contradiction many women know well. Women in leadership are often expected to be decisive but not too forceful, caring but not too soft, confident but never difficult. Yet in a world shaped by burnout, polarisation, inequality and institutional distrust, the old model of leadership as toughness without tenderness looks increasingly out of date. Can women lead with both heart and mind? The answer is yes; and that may be exactly the kind of leadership our institutions now need.

title: Tekoäly muuttaa rekrytoinnin ja työnhaun tapoja
content:
Tekoälyä hyödynnetään yhä enemmän sekä rekrytoinnissa että työnhaussa. Ratkaisevaa on, mihin tarkoitukseen tekoälyä käytetään ja millainen vaikutus sillä on hakijan asemaan.

Rekrytointi, eli uuden työntekijän etsiminen ja valinta, rakentuu tyypillisesti useista toisiinsa kytkeytyvistä vaiheista, joissa tavoitetaan potentiaalisia hakijoita, kootaan ja arvioidaan tietoa heidän osaamisestaan sekä tehdään päätöksiä siitä, ketkä etenevät prosessissa. Tekoälyä hyödynnetään näissä vaiheissa monin tavoin ChatGPT:n kaltaisten yleiskäyttöisten generatiivisen tekoälyn palvelujen avulla sekä digitaalisiin rekrytointipalveluihin sisäänrakennetuilla toiminnoilla.

Tekoälyn käyttö rekrytoinnissa voi vaikuttaa huomattavasti ihmisten uramahdollisuuksiin ja toimeentuloon. Tämän vuoksi Euroopan unionin tekoälyasetus luokittelee osan rekrytointiin tarkoitetusta tekoälystä suuririskiseksi.

title: University libraries between cost-cutting measures and open access transformation
content: From Google's English:  “When considering the financial resources of university libraries, two fundamental developments must be distinguished, both of which impact their budgets,” explains André Karliczek, Deputy Director of the Thuringian University and State Library Jena (ThULB). “Firstly, these libraries, whose core mission is providing information for study, research, and teaching, are increasingly becoming the primary bearers of publication costs in the course of the open access transformation – particularly within the framework of the DEAL agreements – because publishers have shifted their business model from subscription to open access publication. Acquisition budgets are therefore no longer solely used to purchase and license literature, but increasingly also to finance publication fees. Secondly, the changed economic conditions imposed by the federal and state governments necessitate the management of reduced expenditures – though to very different degrees depending on the specific area of ​​responsibility and the federal state.”

title: Watch a Band Perform the Sound Effects from Pink Floyd’s “Money,” Using a Money Counter, Torn Sheets of Paper & More
content:
When Pink Floyd recorded “Money” in 1972, Roger Waters spliced into the opening moments the sounds of cash registers, tearing paper, and jingling coins. Half a century later, the German drummer Sina Doering and her band performed those sounds live, using a bowl of loose change, a toy register, a money counter, and a sheet of paper torn on the beat. And they did it all live at Abbey Road Studios, the same place where Pink Floyd recorded Dark Side of the Moon (on which “Money” appears). Watch it above, and enjoy.

title: Zuckerberg warns against centralizing AI power
content:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg on Monday passionately defended the use of artificial intelligence, as the rapid advancement of the technology faces increased scrutiny — and calls for regulation — in the U.S. and globally.

In a 6,500 word post timed to the announcement of his company’s new open source version of its own model, Muse Spark, Zuckerberg detailed his vision for AI, arguing the technology is not to be feared and pushing back on concerns that superintelligence could strip people of jobs.

“The notion that AI is so dangerous that the only safe path is an extreme concentration of power seems inherently problematic,” Zuckerberg wrote. “Historically, hoping that an absolute power will benevolently provide for humanity if sufficiently enlightened has not led to safe or positive outcomes.”

Zuckerberg’s vision is a direct contrast to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s, who has previously warned how AI could cause job disruption. Meta lags behind Anthropic and OpenAI, which have the most advanced AI models.

title: Cocoa farmers in southeast Cameroon are adapting to EU regulations, but they still want a fair price
content:
The European Union regulation on deforestation-free cocoa will be implemented next year

Originally published on Global Voices

Cocoa farm in Ekombitie. Photo by Leocadia Bongen, used with permission.

Forty cooperative cocoa farmers gathered at the chief’s home, under an iron-roofed shed in Ekombitie village within Cameroon’s South Region, Dja-et-Lobo. Occasionally, the meeting on agroforestry best practices was interrupted by the noise and hooting of passing timber trucks. Judging by the sad expressions on their faces, the farmers were concerned about the price of cocoa, which has fallen drastically since early 2025 and began dropping dramatically in early 2026.

They are aware that a European Union regulation on deforestation-free cocoa will be implemented next year, and are trying to adapt despite doubts about whether the price will rebound. EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) mandates that certain products, including all cocoa and cocoa products imported into the EU, must be deforestation-free, fully traceable, and legally produced.

title: Indigenous Farmer in Indonesia Acquitted in Coal Mining Case
content:
Indonesia’s Supreme Court on August 5 upheld the acquittal of Misran Toni, an Indigenous Dayak farmer known as Imis, who was participating in a coal mining protest and charged with stabbing other protesters in East Kalimantan. 

The case has its roots in the coal mining in Kalimantan that has long been linked to concerns about community safety, deforestation, and environmental degradation. For decades, Dayak communities in Kalimantan have opposed the mining projects. 

A dispute over the use of public roads to haul coal erupted in Muara Kate village, where as many as 100 coal trucks passed daily. In October 2024, after a truck rolled backward and overturned, killing a young pastor, Dayak villagers, including Imis, protested by setting up a camp to stop the trucks. They alleged that the authorities had failed to enforce regulations restricting coal transportation on village roads.

In November 2024, two villagers sleeping in the protest camp were stabbed at about 4 a.m.; one died while the other was severely wounded. Police alleged that they found blood matching one of the victims on Imis’ shirt and in November 2025 prosecutors charged him with murder and placed him in pretrial detention.

title: What types of social interactions benefit people with social anxiety the most?
content:
Human life unfolds through two fundamental modes of being: with others and alone. Social interactions permeate everyday life, and whether brief or prolonged, deep or superficial, face-to-face or online, these exchanges are the building blocks of our relationships. They play a vital role in our psychological and emotional wellbeing.

Contemporary research shows that the key to a rich social life is not how many interactions we have, but how meaningful and positive they are. It also suggests that the quality of a social interaction depends on both situational and individual factors, and how they combine.

Situational factors are the context that surrounds an interaction – whether it occurs face-to-face or virtually, in small or large groups, and with familiar or unfamiliar partners. Individual factors, such as personality traits, reflect the unique characteristics of the people involved.

With loneliness fast becoming a major mental health crisis, it is vital that we learn more about how to build meaningful relationships. Amid this panorama, people with social anxiety offer particularly useful insight into the way socialising works.

Lounaalle osallistuvat Baltic Sea Action Groupin puheenjohtaja Ilkka Herlin ja hallituksen jäsen Saara Kankaanrinta, John Nurmisen säätiön toimitusjohtaja Annamari Arrakoski-Engardt, Åbo Akademin apulaisprofessori Christoffer Boström, Saaristomeren UNESCO-biosfäärialueen koordinaattori Katja Bonnevier, Turun yliopiston dosentti, Saaristomeren tutkimuslaitoksen johtaja Jari Hänninen sekä Paraisten kaupunginjohtaja Tom Simola.

content:
By Azza Karam*

KARBALA, Iraq | 10 August 2026 (IDN) —There are pilgrimages, and then there is Arbaeen.

Each year, millions of people converge on the Iraqi city of Karbala in one of the largest annual religious gatherings anywhere in the world. This year, according to the Governor of Karbala, more than 22 million pilgrims entered the city, including some five million from outside Iraq. Many travelled enormous distances; countless thousands made the final journey on foot. They came to commemorate a death that occurred almost fourteen centuries ago—and to affirm that what that death represented remains profoundly relevant today.

“Arbaeen” means forty in Arabic. It falls on the twentieth day of Safar in the Islamic calendar, forty days after Ashura, which commemorates the martyrdom of Hussayn ibn Ali, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad, at the Battle of Karbala in 680 CE.

title: Beyond metric reductionism: assessment creep as an emerging risk of research evaluation reform | Research Evaluation | Oxford Academic
content: Abstract:  Recent research assessment reforms have successfully challenged the overreliance on simplistic quantitative indicators and promoted broader approaches to evaluation. This paper argues that these reforms may also generate a new risk: assessment creep, understood as the gradual accumulation of evaluation criteria without sufficient attention to how they are prioritised and combined. While criteria such as open science, societal impact, international collaboration, leadership, and mentoring may each be valuable, their proliferation can reduce transparency and make evaluation systems more difficult to understand and scrutinise. Less transparent systems may also make it harder to distinguish legitimate expert judgement from arbitrary decision-making and to detect favouritism or other forms of unwarranted advantage. Drawing on recent debates surrounding responsible research assessment, the paper suggests that the next challenge is not choosing between metrics and expert judgement, but designing evaluation systems that remain coherent, transparent, and accountable as they become increasingly complex.

title: Can We Gamify That? The Innovators Turning Investigations on Spying Scandals and Vote Rigging into Video Games
content:
An animated phone vibrates on a blackened screen as ominous piano music tinkles in the background. When you click, speech bubbles appear. “It’s Thanasis Koukakis,” the person on the other end says. “I’m borrowing a phone… Just don’t try to reach out to me for now. Texts, calls, try to avoid it.”

This is the opening scene of “Predatorgate,” a new video game based on an investigation into the Predator spyware scandal in Greece. Koukakis was the reporter at the heart of that real-life story who discovered his phone had been infected with the highly invasive spyware. This narrative game is based on the investigation by Inside Story, and shows what it’s like to be in the shoes of a journalist under threat of illegal surveillance. In the game — which takes an estimated 30 minutes to play — Koukakis is a colleague who discovers his phone has been targeted.

title: TOP 2025: An update to the Transparency and Openness Promotion Guidelines - PhilPapers
content: Abstract: BackgroundTransparency and openness are core scientific values that enable independent verification of reported research results. The Transparency and Openness Promotion (TOP) Guidelines, first published in 2015 (TOP 2015), provided a flexible framework for journals to design and implement publication standards promoting these values. Over the past decade, widespread use of TOP 2015 contributed to valuable evidence and feedback for refinement.Main TextThe TOP Advisory Board undertook a comprehensive update of TOP 2015 that went into effect in 2025 (TOP 2025). The update introduces an explicit conceptual framework clarifying its primary objective: improving the verifiability of empirical research claims. Standards are reorganized into three categories (Research Practices, Verification Practices, and Verification Studies) that resolve conceptual and structural limitations of TOP 2015. title: ‘I’ve definitely lost followers’: influencers face backlash over Meta ‘pervert glasses’ content
content:
Using ‘spy glasses’ made by Facebook owner leads to floods of negative comments, say content creators

It was hardly an offensive video. Amid the buzz of the Tour de France finale, Oliver Hooson filmed himself whipping up a delicious-looking flat white for a fellow cycling enthusiast. But after posting the footage on social media, the comments that soon rolled in were a real shock. “PERV,” read one. “Out here pushing creep glasses,” said another. His mistake? Documenting the moment with Meta’s “spy glasses”.

Despite being marketed as the latest must-have gadget, Meta’s smartglasses, which can record video footage while being worn, have faced a vicious backlash, particularly relating to concerns about surveillance. There are widespread fears about the glasses being used to film people, especially women, without their consent, and the resultant footage being posted on social media. This has earned them the label of “pervert glasses”, and content creators, no matter how they are used, have faced a flood of negative comments for deploying them.

title: Costa Rican diplomat emerges as strong contender to be first female head of UN
content:
Rebeca Grynspan seen as continuity candidate with tacit support from current secretary general, António Guterres

A Costa Rican diplomat and former vice-president whose parents were refugees from the Holocaust has become the surprise frontrunner to lead the United Nations as its first female secretary general.

Rebeca Grynspan, whose parents emigrated to Central America from Poland – and whose maternal grandparents were killed by the Nazis – is the current head of the UN conference on trade and development (UNCTAD), a body that has exhaustively tallied the economic damage inflicted by Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories.

title: Defending Our Lands and Environment: Protecting the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Worldwide
content:
Statement on International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples

Each year on 9 August, the international community marks the International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, honouring the first session of the UN Working Group on Indigenous Populations in 1982. This year, the CIVICUS global alliance of civil society organisations and activists dedicated to strengthening citizen action around the world reaffirms our solidarity with the more than 476 million Indigenous peoples across 90 countries. They continue to defend lands, cultures, and ways of life in the face of escalating threats.

Indigenous peoples are among the most effective guardians of the world's remaining biodiversity, safeguarding an estimated 80% of it on lands they steward, despite formally holding rights to only a fraction of the territory traditionally occupied. Yet Indigenous human rights defenders and environmental activists who defend these lands remain among the most targeted civil society actors on the planet.
snippet: Statement on International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples

title: Australia’s Albanese Should Press Vietnam’s Leader on Rights
content:
As Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese meets with To Lam, Vietnam’s president and general secretary of the Communist Party, in Canberra this week, he shouldn’t forget that he is dealing with one of the region’s most repressive leaders.

While minister of Vietnam’s notorious Ministry of Public Security from 2016 to 2024, To Lam oversaw a far-reaching crackdown that decimated the country’s budding civil society. Authorities imprisoned dozens of prominent independent journalists, bloggers, and activists, including Pham Doan Trang, Pham Chi Dung, Nguyen Tuong Thuy, Nguyen Lan Thang, and Can Thi Theu. The crackdown also targeted environmentalists and lawyers, many of whom now live in exile for fear of persecution.

Since To Lam ascended to Vietnam’s highest political office as Communist Party general secretary in 2024, the country’s poor human rights record has worsened. The authorities have expanded the scope and use of draconian laws that criminalize free speech. People now risk up to seven years in prison simply for raising complaints about government policies or local officials.

title: Netanyahu’s Challengers Are Selling The Same Poison
content:
By Alon Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 9 August 2026 (IDN) — The men who could replace Netanyahu know the truth and refuse to say it. A Palestinian state is not an existential threat to Israel; the endless denial of one is. By reciting the old lie for votes, Israel’s opposition is not offering a new chapter—it is deepening the catastrophe.

One would think that after 7 October and the Gaza war that followed, the leaders from the main opposition parties would have drawn the obvious conclusion. Eighty years of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict have not made Israel safer. It has made Israel strategically weaker, lonelier, and more reviled than at any moment in its history. Yet the two men most likely to replace Benjamin Netanyahu—former IDF Chief Gadi Eisenkot and, less likely, Naftali Bennett—have already announced what they will not do, nor even imply: take any significant measure to mitigate this endemically self-consuming conflict toward a permanent solution.

title: How a Diamond Open Access Publisher Expanded into Open Textbooks - Pressbooks
content:
The University of Groningen Press (UGP) is a Diamond Open Access university press based in the Netherlands and a member of the Netherlands University Presses (NUPs) network. Since its founding in 2017, the press has supported the publication of Diamond Open Access scholarly journals and books.

In 2021, UGP expanded into a closely related—but distinct—area of open publishing by launching an open textbook pilot. As part of the University’s broader commitment to open education and open science, the initiative explored how UGP could apply its scholarly publishing expertise and open infrastructure to help faculty create high-quality open textbooks and other open educational resources.

What began as a pilot has since developed into an institutional service supporting multiple models of textbook production, enabling collaboration across institutions, and supporting the creation of interactive learning materials designed for teaching and learning contexts.

content: How can science and knowledge production become more open, inclusive and equitable? This is not only a question of access to existing knowledge, but also of agency: who formulates research questions, who is recognised as a knowledge producer, and which forms of knowledge are considered legitimate? During the Netherlands National Open Science Week, Leiden University’s three UNESCO Chairs will come together to discuss these questions. The Chairs maintain broad international networks and collaborate with researchers and knowledge communities in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Their work covers diversity in science, digital diversity, colonial history, and collaboration with societal and international knowledge communities. The central question of the panel is how researchers, universities and research funders can contribute to more equitable international collaboration. The panellists will also critically examine the distribution of resources, authorship, theoretical authority and institutional recognition. content: Abstract: Introduction: Technological advancements and the intensification of information production pose new challenges for information management, requiring tools capable of organizing, preserving, and disseminating knowledge in digital environments. Institutional repositories (IRs) are strategic for systematizing large volumes of documents, promoting access, interoperability, and transparency in information. Although widely used in academia, it is necessary to understand their applicability in other organizational contexts. title: Risks and possibilities in sharing preprints during the doctorate - University of Southern Denmark
content: Abstract:  During doctoral candidature, students may seek to publish journal articles, which they may incorporate in their thesis if their institutional policy permits. They may consider sharing pre-prints of these texts either pre- or post-publication to promote open access and knowledge mobilisation. There is very little extant research that explores doctoral students’ knowledge of the risks and possibilities involved in sharing their work in this form, and this chapter seeks to identify those that they could encounter. It offers immediate value for informing doctoral education and a useful foundation for future research that is specific to the doctoral student experience.

title: Catholicos Garegin II in court
content:
By Benoit Lannoo*

YEREVAN, Armenia | 8 August 2026 (IDN) — Do you remember the Investiture Controversy, when medieval emperors tried to take over the pope’s episcopal appointments? Or the difficult issue of the appointment of bishops in the People’s Republic of China? Well, although Armenia is considered a democratic state in Western chancelleries, respectful of the rule of law, an unprecedented Church-State conflict is currently raging.

Yesterday, ‘His Holiness Garegin II, Patriarch of Etchmiadzin and Catholicos of All Armenians’, together with six other higher clerics, had to appear before a court of first instance in the provincial capital of Armavir because earlier this year he withdrew the episcopal title of Gevorg Saroyan, former primate of the diocese of Masyatsotn, and brought Saroyan later even back to the lay state, and the Catholicos refuses to reverse his decision. ‘Abuse of power’ is the accusation.

Imagine what would happen if Pope Leo XIV were cited to appear before a lower court in Los Angeles because the Trump Administration disagrees with a bishop’s appointment over there…

title: Why finance jobs are widening income inequality in cities around the world
content:
Try to imagine the history of New York without Wall Street, or London without the City. It’s not easy.

Hosting a country’s main financial markets shapes a city’s identity, raises its profile and creates jobs. But there are trade-offs. By acting as a magnet for high-paying finance jobs and related professions, many financial cities suffer from particularly high levels of income inequality.

In fact, alongside globalisation and the clustering of highly skilled workers, our research has found that the presence of a financial market is a major driver of the growing concentration of top earners and earnings inequality in select cities.

In a study conducted by two dozen researchers, we examined top earnings in cities in 10 countries across Europe, North America and Asia, analysing two decades of linked employer-employee data.

For every country studied, we compare two cities: the financial hub housing the main national markets and related industries, and a second, comparison city that is closest in terms of population, employment and share of GDP.

title: The Crisis of Scholarly Communication in the Open Access Environment: Pathways to Diamond Open Access[v1] | Preprints.org
content: Abstract: This paper presents a critical analysis of the current system of scholarly communication, which has undergone a profound transformation under the influence of excessive commercialization within the neoliberal "publish or perish" paradigm. The study demonstrates that the Open Access movement, in its current form, has been co-opted by major commercial publishers through mechanisms such as Article Processing Charges (APCs) and "Transformative Agreements," which fail to solve the problem of creating a fair and accessible environment for the dissemination of knowledge. The work substantiates the thesis that the prestige of academic journals has ceased to be a reliable indicator of scientific quality, and that the traditional peer-review system is in a state of crisis, driven by the exponential growth of publications and a catastrophic shortage of qualified reviewers. The author analyzes potential solutions to this impasse, including a transition to platform-based publication and review models, as well as the advancement of Diamond Open Access. title: Who Owns Discovery? Academic Capitalism, Prestige Markets, and the Enclosure of Science
content: Abstract: Academic publishing rests on an institutional paradox that borders on the absurd. Public institutions finance much of the research and universities pay the scientists; those scientists then write the papers and typically supply peer review without compensation from publishers, while publishers often acquire exclusive rights and sell access back to the institutions that provided both the knowledge and the evaluative labor. Smaller universities and peripheral research systems contribute to a global scholarly record that their libraries may struggle to afford, while their researchers face a second barrier when publication itself carries a fee. This article reconstructs how that arrangement emerged through the history of publishing, the sociology of science, industrial organization, research evaluation, open access, and the political economy of artificial intelligence. Necessary infrastructure becomes a source of rent when exclusive rights, non-substitutable catalogues, and brands used to allocate jobs and funding are integrated with data and platforms. title: Examining Persistence of European Open Repository Infrastructure and its Diffusion in the Scholarly Record – InfoDoc MicroVeille
content: "This article seeks to determine the extent to which the principle of persistence is observed by repositories and the organizations that operate them. In addition, the impact that negative repository persistence levels may be having on the scholarly record is assessed. This is achieved by interrogating and combining data on European repositories from several repository registries and web-scraped sources, including the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine, which creates a unique dataset of historic repository locations and their OAI-PMH endpoints. Then, this data is used as the basis for text mining CORE, a vast corpus of scholarly outputs, to determine the extent to which impersistent European repository content has permeated the scholarly literature. title: Asiakkaat pakenevat kuumuutta pihalle
content:
Hellepäivinä lämpötila Helsingin Rikhardinkadun kirjaston korkeimmissa osissa saattaa nousta 30 asteeseen. Silloin ihmiset siirtyvät usein kirjaston sisäpihalle.

Ajatus Rikun kesäpihasta syntyi yli kymmenen vuotta sitten, kun henkilökunta vei kirjaston huonekasvit ulos suihkutettavaksi. Vaikka asfaltoitua sisäpihaa reunustavat joka puolelta talojen seinät, lopputulos näytti silti vehreältä.

”Sisäpihan yläpuolelle on nykyään vielä ripustettu erivärisiä sateenvarjoja”, Rikhardinkadun kirjaston johtaja Juha Kortesluoma kertoo.

Pihan laittaminen ei vaadi kirjaston henkilökunnalta juuri muita resursseja kuin lihaksia.

”Sinne kannetaan kasvit, tuolit ja pöydät, ja sitten se pyörii omalla painollaan.”

Helsingin aluekirjastojen silloinen johtaja Saara Ihamäki sai koronakeväänä 2020 idean, että jokaisella Helsingin viidestä alueesta olisi yksi kesäkirjasto, jossa on kesäpiha ja joka on auki myös kesäviikonloppuisin.

Läntisellä alueella ensimmäiseksi kesäkirjastoksi valikoitui Etelä-Haagan kirjasto. Kirjastotyöntekijä Sari Langdonin mukaan kesäpiha on ollut suosittu siitä lähtien.

title: Skåne dominerar årets Wiki Loves Earth – här är kommunerna med flest bilder
content:
Under maj månad arrangerade Wikimedia Sverige ännu en gång den svenska upplagan av Wiki Loves Earth. Genom tävlingen dokumenterar fotografer skyddad natur och delar sina bilder under fri licens på Wikimedia Commons där de kan användas på bland annat Wikipedia och hjälper till att dokumentera och sprida kunskap om naturen till människor över hela världen. Nu har vi sammanställt statistiken och kan presentera kommunerna som utmärkte sig mest i årets tävling. 

I år deltog 1266 bilder i Wiki Loves Earth – nästan en fördubbling gentemot förra året! Av årets uppladdade bilder kommer en stor del från skånska naturreservat, nationalparker och andra skyddade områden. Kristianstad toppar listan över kommuner med flest uppladdade bilder, tätt följt av Lund. Totalt återfinns fem skånska kommuner på topp 10-listan. Många av de skånska bilderna kommer från den fotosafari Wikimedia Sverige organiserade i Skåne i samarbete med WWF där vi besökte flera skyddade naturområden med särskilt fokus på att dokumentera platser som tidigare saknat bilder helt på Wikimedia Commons.

title: The History of Glam Rock and How It Put an End to the Hippie Era
content:
Cast your mind back to the distant year 2021 and recall, if you will, its music, its fashions, the obsessions of its youth. This probably won’t be a difficult task, since in most respects — the dampening effects of the pandemic notwithstanding — none of those aspects of popular culture seem any different today. Yet roughly the same time span separated Scott McKenzie’s “San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Flowers in Your Hair)” and David Bowie’s “Starman.” 1967 was the year of the Summer of Love; by 1972, according to most reckonings, the cultural era known as the Sixties was, if not quite over, then at least clearly in its final days. The hippies were on their way down, and glam rockers had arisen to take their place with a vengeance.

In less than half an hour, the new video from Bandsplaining tells the whole story of glam rock, “the gender-bending proto-punk movement that was hated by the press and criminally underplayed in the U.S.” It begins in the 1970s, a time when the market for long-playing records was robust, but singles had fallen behind as a youth-oriented pop-cultural form.

title: Bernie Sanders has AI policy all wrong
content:
In December 2025, Senator Bernie Sanders became the first member of Congress to demand a moratorium on the construction of new AI data centers. The costs of the infrastructure that powers generative AI technologies like chatbots and image generators were soaring, but it was not clear that regular people were seeing much benefit. The ban was necessary, Sanders argued, to give “democracy a chance to catch up.”

Sanders could have also said that politicians needed to catch up to the public. Recent polling suggests more than 70 percent of Americans oppose the construction of data centers near their communities. It’s no wonder why: People have been seeing their power bills soar, high-voltage cables rammed through their properties, their water supplies sullied, and their days disrupted by the incessant hum of air conditioners keeping the buildings cool. It’s hard to think of another issue that has so quickly galvanized Americans across the political spectrum.

title: Feeling these heatwaves?
content:
Dear friend ,

It’s been relentless this summer, hasn’t it? These endless heatwaves are a real wake-up call for our councils, showing very clearly that they need to be putting adaptations in place to make our infrastructure more resilient against extreme weather, wildfires and drought.

But don’t sweat. Here’s Isaac from our partners Climate Emergency UK explaining what you can do if you’re feeling powerless in the face of all this heat.

The key is adaptation — the ways in which councils adapt our habitats for resilience, for example by planting more trees, reusing water or making our homes more able to withstand extremes of temperature.

There are useful graphics that explain more on the Council Climate Action Scorecards site. And once you've got that info, take a look to see how your own council is doing, on the main Scorecards section.

While this sun is beating down, it's a great time to go and chat with your councillors about your council's record on adaptation and resilience: why not download these graphics as a conversation-opener?

title: Telecom CEOs blast EU for failing to crack down on child sexual abuse content
content:
Four of Europe’s biggest telecom chiefs are calling for tougher EU powers to help them block child sexual abuse material online and break through national regulatory bottlenecks.

“Children need protection now, not in several years’ time,” the CEOs of leading telcos wrote in a letter, obtained by POLITICO and addressed to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, European Parliament President Roberta Metsola and European Council President António Costa.

The signatories of the letter, dated Aug. 6, are Vodafone’s Margherita Della Valle, Orange’s Christel Heydemann, Telenor’s Benedicte Schilbred Fasmer and BT’s Allison Kirkby.

The telecom chiefs want the European Commission to introduce EU-wide administrative orders allowing internet providers to block confirmed illegal content until it is eliminated. The letter also calls for the creation of a new EU watchdog with “legal authority” to maintain a database of indicators of CSAM that could serve as the basis for enforcement action.

title: Liberia Ends Primary School Registration Fees
content:
Liberia’s government announced on August 5 the elimination of all school registration fees from kindergarten through grade 6, beginning with the new school year on September 7. The decision removes one of the biggest barriers to schooling for hundreds of thousands of children.

A recent Human Rights Watch report, “Without Education, There Will Be Nothing,” documents that school registration fees have often placed schooling out of reach or imposed severe hardship, particularly for low-income and rural families. Human Rights Watch found that fees forced many children out of school altogether. Others started years late, attended irregularly, or engaged in child labor to help pay their fees. One-third of Liberian children have never attended school, and only 17 percent completed grade 9.

Parents told Human Rights Watch that they went into debt, skipped meals, and made extraordinary sacrifices to pay fees at public schools. Beatrice, a 17-year-old from Nimba County, said she was forced to leave school when her parents could not afford her registration fees. “I felt bad,” she said. “I stayed home and cried when I saw my friends going to school.”

title: What is UN Peacebuilding Week? Q&A with CMI’s Natalia Martinez Cutillas
content:
In June this year CMI attended the UN’s first Peacebuilding Week in New York. But why was CMI invited and how does attendance support the organisation’s goals? We spoke to Natalia Martinez Cutillas of CMI’s Multilateral Affairs and Peacemaking Policy team to find out more.

Natalia Martinez Cutillas: When the UN Peacebuilding Architecture was established in 2005, Member States agreed that it should be reviewed every five years to ensure it remained fit for purpose. This process, known as the UN Peacebuilding Architecture Review (PBAR), most recently took place in 2025. As part of the outcome of that review, Member States mandated that an annual UN Peacebuilding Week should be organised.

The idea behind the week was to shine a spotlight on the UN’s peacebuilding work, build political support for peacebuilding efforts, create space for inclusive dialogue and showcase good practices from around the world.

title: Alleged ‘Enforcer’ in Prince Group Scam Network Identified
content:
An individual identified as “Co-Conspirator-2” in a U.S. grand jury indictment allegedly acted as an “enforcer” for the Prince Group by fending off police crackdowns on the  sprawling Cambodian conglomerate accused of running major cyber scams.

The indictment did not disclose the identity of Co-Conspirator-2, but it contained enough personal information for reporters to confirm that the person is Chen Sokly, who was born in China and has lived in the U.S. and Singapore. 

The indictment targets Prince Group Chairman Chen Zhi, who is charged with alleged wire fraud and money laundering conspiracy. Chen Zhi was extradited from Cambodia to China where he also faces charges. The U.S. court documents obtained by OCCRP do not show any plea, and a spokesperson for the District Court for the Eastern District of New York declined to provide an update on the status of the case. 

A spokesperson for the Prince Group rejected the U.S. Justice Department’s allegations, telling OCCRP they would “challenge these accusations [and] expose the factual and chronological impossibilities on which they rest.”

In the indictment, U.S. prosecutors cited seven anonymized co-conspirators.

title: House Democrats Demand Answers From Trump’s VA on Vets Struggling to Access Mental Healthcare
content:
What Happened: More than 60 House Democrats are pressing Department of Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins for answers about how the agency’s mental healthcare has been increasingly strained under President Donald Trump’s second administration. The lawmakers sent the secretary a letter last week asking questions about the state of VA care, citing a ProPublica investigation from this spring that revealed the agency’s mental health workforce has been plummeting and veterans have been left in the lurch.

What They Said: The letter was spearheaded by Rep. Judy Chu, who is a psychologist and represents a district in Southern California. “Caring for our nation’s Veterans is a fundamental responsibility,” the letter says. “That includes ensuring access to high-quality mental health care.”

The lawmakers demanded that the VA disclose details about its shortage of mental health providers and the impact on veterans. It also pushed the agency to lay out how long veterans have to wait for care.

content:
Yaser tarkistaa joka päivä ennen töihin lähtöään, toimiiko internet. Hän ei tee sitä itsensä vaan 18-vuotiaan tyttärensä Mariamin vuoksi. Mariam ei ole voinut käydä koulua viiteen vuoteen – mutta hän voi edelleen opiskella verkossa, kunhan internet toimii.

title: Europe’s wildfires have raised the danger posed by unexploded WWII bombs
content:
When a wildfire broke out in the Müritz National Park of north-eastern Germany in July, it was no routine firefighting job. Bomb disposal teams had to work alongside firefighters because the forest floor is contaminated with cold war-era munitions. Crews could not approach parts of the blaze directly for fear of detonations.

Soon after, a wildfire tore through 42,000 hectares of the Gironde region in south-western France. As it burned through fields near the village of Le Porge, the fire exposed a forgotten cache of second world war-era shells. At least 75 were recovered from the scorched earth.

Several of the shells had detonated during the fire and one projectile punched through the wall of a house that had been evacuated. The local mayor, Martial Zaninetti, said the municipality had no record the munitions were there at all.

These events are symptoms of a clear problem: Europe is full of buried explosives left over from 20th century wars, and the continent’s wildfires are now big enough, hot enough and last long enough to reach them.

title: Ships stuck in the Strait of Hormuz region may be biosecurity risks when they leave. What can we do?
content:
The economic ramifications of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz are much discussed. But so far, the risk of ecological damage following a long blockade of ships has been overlooked.

Our recent research shows the more than 1,500 commercial vessels that have been laid up in the Persian/Arabian Gulf since February pose a significant environmental threat because they have been accumulating marine biofouling species on their hulls.

As the strait reopens, these ships may spread these organisms to ports they visit, potentially causing an international biosecurity “super-spreader” event.

Such incursions of alien marine plants, animals, parasites and diseases affect native ecosystems and wild fisheries as well as aquaculture stocks and coastal industries. They can lead to significant environmental damage and economic losses.

But the closure of the Strait of Hormuz is not the first time shipping disruptions have resulted in significant biofouling on idle vessels.

Global merchant vessel traffic is the main mode of transport for commodities, and researchers have identified 24 choke points in maritime trade.

title: From The Trap Of Geopolitics To A Geo-Civilizational Paradigm
content:
“Nation-states are a Western invention, naturally vulnerable to Western influence. Civilizations are an alternative to the West,” the Portuguese diplomat and scholar Bruno Maçães has written in Noema.

In his new book for Berggruen Press, “In Search Of Greater India,” Maçães explores what the light of Indian civilization that existed millennia before the advent of the nation-state might teach the modern West — and the rest of the world its dominance shaped for centuries.

He cites Carl Jung on the unenlightened and insecure person as an analogue for the national ego, which “projects the traits they repress or reject in themselves onto others, who as a result are transformed into convenient repositories of everything evil and ugly in the human personality. This is how world politics becomes a final confrontation between good and evil. The monsters we confront are the monsters we ourselves have created. And since they are all too ready to destroy us, we must be ready to destroy them. Until that final moment, one must wait, perhaps responsibly, but life is already haunted by annihilation.”
